tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

You are producing a cinematic, beat-synced music visualizer MP4 for ONE song. Three other agents are doing other songs in parallel on the same machine (shared GPU), so be economical with preview renders.

SONG: "/Users/vojta/Downloads/voho/Bad Boys.wav" (234.0 s, 44.1 kHz stereo)

SHARED VENV (already built, do NOT run setup.sh): REDACTED
SKILL DIR (SK): /Users/vojta/.claude/skills/music-visualizer

Environment: GPU rendering (stills, clips, full render) needs the Bash sandbox disabled (dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true) — moderngl fails with "cannot choose pixel format" inside it. Analysis/verification can run sandboxed. Run the full render in the background. Writing into /Users/vojta/Downloads/voho also needs the sandbox off.

Title/artist: use file tags if present; otherwise title = "Bad Boys", artist = "voho".

Creative brief (from the user): an official-visualizer-quality piece by an exceptionally talented motion designer, fully driven by the music, visually surprising first frame to last. Listen first: tempo/beat grid, downbeats, onsets (kick/snare/hats), band energies, loudness, section structure — write the section timestamps into mapping.md and base the edit on them. Kick/bass -> scale, pulses, camera punches, shockwaves; snare -> cuts, flashes, reveals; hats/highs -> particles, sparkle; mids/vocals -> fluid motion, color shifts, typography; energy -> density/speed/brightness. Cuts on downbeats/phrase boundaries only. Builds visibly build; drops hit hard; quiet sections breathe. Kinetic typography for title/artist; mix 3D geometry, fluid, particles, distortion, masking, DOF, camera moves. One cohesive identity (palette, type, ONE recurring motif) derived from THIS song's mood/genre, evolved across sections; bridge = surprising shift in perspective/palette/scale; outro resolves the motif to a clean title/artist lockup final frame. Do NOT just reskin the arcade example — give this song its own distinct world and motif (the other three songs are getting their own looks too). Photosensitivity-safe flashes, title-safe text, dithered gradients.

Tech: 1920x1080, 60 fps (30 only if unavoidable), H.264 yuv420p CRF 18, AAC 320k 48 kHz, duration exactly matches the song, audio sync verified at start/middle/end (verify_sync.py pass criteria in SKILL.md).

DELIVERABLES: copy the final MP4 to "/Users/vojta/Downloads/voho/Bad Boys - visualizer.mp4" and the notes to "/Users/vojta/Downloads/voho/Bad Boys - visualizer NOTES.md" (notes: detected BPM, section timestamps, audio-feature -> visual mapping, verification results).

Your final message must report: output paths, BPM, section list with timestamps, the visual identity/motif in 2-3 sentences, verify_sync results (peak lags, audio alignment at start/mid/end, max flashes/s), and any caveats or failed checks, stated honestly.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

I checked every MP4: 1920×1080 at 60 fps, H.264 yuv420p at CRF 18, and AAC at 48 kHz (about 320 kbps). Each video's length matches its song to within one frame. | Night Blur | 107 | A night motorway through a camera viewfinder, with a 7-blade aperture as the motif | 77% | 2 |

Each notes file lists the section timestamps and which audio features drive which visuals.

Things you should know:
- **Beat hits are below target.** Every video shows a visible hit on only about 75–78% of beats, against the aim of close to 100%. The misses cluster in the quiet or kick-less stretches (bridges, intros, outro fades). The drops score close to 100%.
- **Two videos were re-rendered for flashes.** The first full renders of Night Blur and Ngizula broke the flash limit (4 and 6 flashes per second). Both were toned down and re-rendered, so their drops hit a little less hard than the first versions did.
- **The analysis script needed patches for every song.** The bundled analysis crashed or cut the songs into wrong sections, mostly because kicks under heavy sub bass weren't detected. Each agent fixed this in its own copy of the script. The shared skill is unchanged, and all timestamps still come from the audio. These fixes are worth folding back into the skill.
- **Files are larger than your suggested bitrate.** They run 19–26 Mbps (555–728 MB) rather than 12–16 Mbps, because CRF 18 plus film grain produces more data. YouTube accepts this. If you'd rather have smaller files, I can re-encode to a 16 Mbps cap.
- **Minor:** in Bad Boys, the snare detector misses about half the snares in the drops, so the siren beams there also fire on beats 2 and 4 by the grid. In Night Blur, snare and hi-hat visuals land one frame after the sound.

The scene code and analysis for each song are in the session scratchpad under `viz/<song>/` if you want to change anything.

27	| `references/analysis.md` | how the analysis works, the pitfalls it already handles, how to fix a wrong tempo/downbeat/section |
28	| `references/engine.md` | API reference for timeline / gfx / vfont / render, post parameters, performance numbers, rendering gotchas |

32	
33	`SK` = this skill's directory, `W` = a work directory (for example the scratchpad). All commands run from anywhere.
34	
35	### 1. Setup and analysis (about 1 minute)
36	```bash
37	bash $SK/scripts/setup.sh W                          # once per machine/work dir
38	W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/analyze.py "song.mp3" --workdir W
39	W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/inspect_analysis.py --workdir W --zoom 60,64   # then Read W/analysis.png
40	```
41	Check the printout and the PNG, not raw JSON. Section boundaries should sit on audible changes (the band curves step there), the downbeat lines should carry the big transitions, and the zoom row should show kicks on the red beat lines.
42	If something is off (tempo octave, downbeat phase, a missed or extra section), read `references/analysis.md`; the fixes are parameter-level.
43	Title and artist come from the file tags (`--title/--artist` override). The cover art is often embedded: `ffmpeg -i song.mp3 -an -c:v copy W/cover.jpg`. Look at it before designing.
44

46	Read `references/design-playbook.md`. Decide and write down in `W/mapping.md`:
47	- the identity: 4-6 palette colors (linear RGB), ONE motif that recurs in every section, a type treatment
48	- the audio -> visual table (kick / snare / hat / beat / downbeat / phrase / sub / mids / highs / loudness / section)
49	- one treatment per section type, and how each repeat escalates (drop 1 < drop 2 < finale)
50	
51	### 3. Scene module
52	Copy `examples/scene_arcade.py` to `W/scene.py` and re-art-direct it. Keep its structural patterns (they are what makes sync exact): the highway depth mapping, envelopes from `timeline.py`, cyclic motion from `beatpos` at 1/4-4 beats per cycle, phrase-indexed camera changes, the iris transition on section starts, HUD on its own layer.
53	Contract: `class Scene(tl, eng)` with `render(f)`; optional `fluid(f)` for warm-up. See `references/engine.md`.
54	
55	### 4. Look development with stills (cheap)
56	```bash
57	W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/render.py --workdir W --scene W/scene.py --stills 12,40.3,55,76,100,131,170,203.5
58	W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/contact_sheet.py W/stills W/sheet.png 4       # Read one image
59	```
60	Pick one still per section, plus drop starts about 2 frames in. Iterate here until every section reads. The usual first-pass problems and their fixes are in `references/engine.md` under "Gotchas".
61	
62	### 5. Debug preview of the most complex section
63	```bash
64	W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/render.py --workdir W --scene W/scene.py --start 138 --end 158 --debug --preset veryfast --out W/debug.mp4
65	```
66	The overlay shows the scrolling beat/downbeat grid, typed onsets, section labels, bar.beat, band meters and onset lamps.
67	Pull a filmstrip around a drop (`ffmpeg -i W/debug.mp4 -vf "select='between(n,N-3,N+4)',scale=480:270" -vsync 0 W/strip/f_%02d.png`, then contact-sheet it). The drop must change on the frame nearest its timestamp, together with the kick lamp.
68	
69	### 6. Verify on a clean clip, then render everything
70	```bash
71	W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/render.py --workdir W --scene W/scene.py --start 138 --end 158 --preset veryfast --out W/clip.mp4
72	W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/verify_sync.py --workdir W --video W/clip.mp4 --offset 138
73	W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/render.py --workdir W --scene W/scene.py --out W/final.mp4    # run in background
74	W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/verify_sync.py --workdir W --video W/final.mp4
75	W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/make_notes.py --workdir W --video W/final.mp4 --mapping W/mapping.md --out W/NOTES.md
76	```
77	Pass criteria: kick, beat and section `peak_lag == 0`; audio-vs-source lag 0 samples at start, middle and end; `max_flashes_per_second <= 3`; beats with a visible hit close to 100% in non-silent passages. Deliver the MP4 and NOTES.md next to the source song, or wherever the user asks.
78	
79	## Environment notes
80	- **GPU needs the sandbox off.** On macOS, `moderngl.create_standalone_context()` fails inside the Claude Code sandbox with "cannot choose pixel format". Run render, stills and smoke tests with the sandbox disabled. Analysis and verification run fine sandboxed.
81	- **Speed.** On an M1 Max a 1080p60 render runs at about 20-28 fps (libx264 `slow`, CRF 18), so a 3.5-minute song takes about 10 minutes. Always run the full render in the background.
82	- The output is H.264 High, yuv420p, BT.709 tv-range tags, CRF 18, AAC 320k 48 kHz, `+faststart`. Grain plus TPDF dither in the final shader prevents banding.
83	
84	## Rules that keep it honest (and why)
85	- **Every moving parameter reads the timeline.** Cyclic motion uses `tl.beatpos` (phase-locked); non-cyclic drift uses `tl.flow` or highway travel scaled by `tl.activity`, so silence means stillness. Never use a raw clock. That is what makes a muted viewer able to tap along.
86	- **Hits happen on the transient frame.** Envelopes jump on the frame nearest the event and only decay afterwards. Beats are snapped to kick transients, so kick, beat and section visuals share a frame. Do not smooth event envelopes; smooth only continuous bands (fast attack, slow release).
87	- **The highway trick.** Place anything that "arrives" at depth `D(te) - D(t) + ZS`, where `D` is integrated travel. It crosses the strike plane exactly when it sounds, at any speed, including during accelerating builds.
88	- **Transitions land on the boundary frame.** Start iris wipes and surges at `sec_time == 0`. Anticipation (a build's suction, countdowns) may precede the boundary, but the change itself may not.
89	- **Photosensitivity.** Keep full-screen additive flashes tiny (<= 0.02 linear); use exposure surges instead, which keep contrast. Put strobing detail in small elements, and check `max_flashes_per_second`.
90	- **Title-safe.** HUD text stays within 90% of the frame (|x| <= 864, |y| <= 486 px from the centre at 1080p).
91	
92	## Token-saving habits
93	- Review frames via contact sheets and filmstrips, never one PNG per Read.
94	- Print compact tables (`inspect_analysis.py`) instead of dumping JSON.
95	- Edit scene parameters surgically (small python/sed replacements) and re-render only the affected stills.
96	- Do not re-derive the analysis heuristics or the engine. If they fail on a song, fix the specific parameter the references point to.

```bash
W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/verify_sync.py --workdir W --video W/clip.mp4 --offset 138
W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/render.py --workdir W --scene W/scene.py --out W/final.mp4    # run in background
W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/verify_sync.py --workdir W --video W/final.mp4
W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/make_notes.py --workdir W --video W/final.mp4 --mapping W/mapping.md --out W/NOTES.md
```
Pass criteria: kick, beat and section `peak_lag == 0`; audio-vs-source lag 0 samples at start, middle and end; `max_flashes_per_second <= 3`; beats with a visible hit close to 100% in non-silent passages. Deliver the MP4 and NOTES.md next to the source song, or wherever the user asks.

## Environment notes
- **GPU needs the sandbox off.** On macOS, `moderngl.create_standalone_context()` fails inside the Claude Code sandbox with "cannot choose pixel format". Run render, stills and smoke tests with the sandbox disabled. Analysis and verification run fine sandboxed.
- **Speed.** On an M1 Max a 1080p60 render runs at about 20-28 fps (libx264 `slow`, CRF 18), so a 3.5-minute song takes about 10 minutes. Always run the full render in the background.
- The output is H.264 High, yuv420p, BT.709 tv-range tags, CRF 18, AAC 320k 48 kHz, `+faststart`. Grain plus TPDF dither in the final shader prevents banding.

## Rules that keep it honest (and why)
- **Every moving parameter reads the timeline.** Cyclic motion uses `tl.beatpos` (phase-locked); non-cyclic drift uses `tl.flow` or highway travel scaled by `tl.activity`, so silence means stillness. Never use a raw clock. That is what makes a muted viewer able to tap along.
- **Hits happen on the transient frame.** Envelopes jump on the frame nearest the event and only decay afterwards. Beats are snapped to kick transients, so kick, beat and section visuals share a frame. Do not smooth event envelopes; smooth only continuous bands (fast attack, slow release).
- **The highway trick.** Place anything that "arrives" at depth `D(te) - D(t) + ZS`, where `D` is integrated travel. It crosses the strike plane exactly when it sounds, at any speed, including during accelerating builds.
- **Transitions land on the boundary frame.** Start iris wipes and surges at `sec_time == 0`. Anticipation (a build's suction, countdowns) may precede the boundary, but the change itself may not.
- **Photosensitivity.** Keep full-screen additive flashes tiny (<= 0.02 linear); use exposure surges instead, which keep contrast. Put strobing detail in small elements, and check `max_flashes_per_second`.
- **Title-safe.** HUD text stays within 90% of the frame (|x| <= 864, |y| <= 486 px from the centre at 1080p).

## Token-saving habits
- Review frames via contact sheets and filmstrips, never one PNG per Read.
- Print compact tables (`inspect_analysis.py`) instead of dumping JSON.
- Edit scene parameters surgically (small python/sed replacements) and re-render only the affected stills.
- Do not re-derive the analysis heuristics or the engine. If they fail on a song, fix the specific parameter the references point to.

# Design playbook

## 1. Identity in 10 minutes
1. **Sources.** The embedded cover art, the title and the genre and mood read from the analysis (tempo, sub weight, brightness from centroid, lead presence, structure). Summarise the mood in 3 words.
2. **Palette.** 1 near-black ground, 2 primaries, 1 highlight for highs, 1 escalation accent held back for the biggest moments. Use linear RGB; line colours around 1.0 bloom nicely.
3. **One motif** that can become everything: HUD element, tunnel gate, sun/horizon object, map, final lockup. Examples: reticle (sci-fi or arcade), ring, chevron, glyph, waveform loop, flower of lines, pixel block, orbit. The motif is what makes separate sections feel like one world.
4. **Type.** The stroke font suits vector, retro-tech and minimal styles (it can glow, draw on and shatter). For other styles, render text to a texture with PIL and composite (add a textured-quad layer), but keep one family.
5. **Camera grammar.** Decide per section: static, push, orbit, fly-over, top-down. Cuts happen only on phrase boundaries; everything else is eased moves driven by phrase progress plus beat-locked sway.

## 2. Audio -> visual mapping (template; fill in per song in mapping.md)
| Audio feature | Visual response (keep it consistent all song) |
|---|---|
| kick | arriving gate hits the strike plane; scale punch (`kick`); camera shake (`kick_fast` x sub); shockwave refraction ring; fluid radial burst |
| snare / clap | panel flash + shape reveal (polygon faces), small exposure surge (never a big full-screen flash) |
| hi-hat | sparks and particle bursts, star twinkle, ticks on the motif, letter reveals |
| beat | every beat ring flares at the strike plane; HUD beat lamps (downbeat larger) |
| downbeat | brighter rings, core ring flash, words arriving |
| phrase (4/8/16 bars) | camera angle cut or roll change, palette hue notch, add a layer |
| section | new visual state via an iris wipe from the motif, landing on the boundary frame, exposure surge + shock |
| sub / bass | mass: tunnel radius and pressure, terrain displacement, FOV breathing, camera shake depth |
| mids / lead | fluid emitters (bar-locked orbits), hue drift by pitch class / centroid, typography weight and brightness |
| highs | sparkle, particle density, star twinkle, edge ticks; a filtered-away top end means defocus |
| loudness | exposure, density, travel speed (`activity`); silence means stillness |

## 3. Section treatments (from the reference scene; reuse and re-skin)
- **Highway tunnel (drops).** Rings on the 16th grid (level-weighted: downbeat > beat > 8th > 16th), each ring's radius shaped by the spectrum at its own time, so the approaching music is visible. Kick gates are motif rings; hat sparks on the walls; snare panels; bass chevrons; speed streaks. Camera roll changes per phrase; beat-locked sway.
- **Spectrogram terrain (choruses).** Rows on the grid and columns as frequency bands (bass far, highs near the road), heights from `spec_s` at each row's time, kick ripple along the ground. A motif "sun" at the horizon carries a spectrum ring. Words arrive on downbeats and shatter on impact. Escalate with a mirrored ceiling (canyon) and the accent colour.
- **Gyroscope core (verses).** Motif rings rotating at 4 / 2 / -4 beats per revolution, an icosahedron that flashes on snares, an equatorial radial spectrum, orbiting particles lit in sequence by hats, an orbit camera that cuts per phrase, strong depth of field.
- **Radar beat clock (bridge).** Top-down view: the sweep turns once per bar, and onsets are plotted at their bar position (radius = type), so the sweep hits each blip as it sounds and phosphor afterglow draws the rhythm's mandala. Monochrome amber palette, the camera rises to reveal scale: a perspective, palette and scale shift in one.
- **Builds.** Travel speed ramps with progress squared (the highway keeps sync), FOV tightens, ticks double each bar, countdown numerals per bar (bars remaining), zoom blur and chromatic aberration rise, the grade warms, a final-beat suction (exposure dip + negative barrel), then the drop.
- **Breakdown (filtered top end).** Aperture and focus follow `1 - high`: the picture loses focus as the filter closes and snaps back as it opens. Desaturate with it.
- **Outro.** Motion amplitude follows `activity` to zero; a lockup (motif + title + artist) draws on over about 1.5 beats and then holds completely still until the end.
- **Intro.** Near-silence is a single pip. The motif draws on over the first bars, hats add ticks, sub swells send pressure rings, and the title types on one letter per hat after the first phrase of 8 s or more, with the artist on the next phrase.

## 4. Escalation of repeats
Same treatment with more of it: more layers from the first frame, a faster travel speed, the escalation accent colour, a mirrored or extra geometry layer, a stronger fluid, a bigger slam word or multiplier ("RUSH", "RUSH x2", "RUSH x3"). Keep the language identical so viewers recognise the repeat.

## 5. Transitions
An iris wipe from the motif's centre (`mix_mode=1, iris_r = ease_out(sec_time / len) * 1.15`) starts exactly on the boundary; its length is 1 beat, or 0.35 beat for drops. Render the previous look into slot 0 and the new one into slot 1 only during the wipe. Add an exposure surge plus a big shock ring on the same frame. Continuity comes from the motif and the shared highway (the verse keeps a dim tunnel behind its core).

## 6. Photosensitivity and polish
- At most 3 flashes per second in any 25%-area region (verified). Additive full-screen flashes should stay at or below 0.02 linear; use exposure surges.
- Avoid saturated red full-screen changes. Keep ember/magenta for small elements.
- Grain about 0.014 plus TPDF dither (already in the final shader) against banding. Use vignette 0.35-0.45 and subtle scanlines (0.03-0.06) for a CRT or vector feel.
- Title-safe: HUD corners at +-820 x +-440 px.
- The final frame must be a clean, readable lockup. Check the last still (t = duration - 0.1).

## Visual identity
Derived from the cover art (a retro sci-fi cockpit with green holographic HUD rings and amber instrument lights) and the track (a 108 BPM four-on-the-floor synth instrumental).
- **Palette:** teal-black void; phosphor green (primary lines); amber (instruments, downbeats, type); cyan for highs and sparks; ember and magenta held back for escalation (drop 2+, chorus 2); white-hot for impacts.
- **Motif:** the **targeting reticle** (rings, ticks, crosshair gaps, centre pip). It is the HUD, every kick gate in the tunnel, the horizon sun, the gyroscope core, the radar, and the final lockup.
- **Type:** a custom chamfered stroke font drawn as glowing vector lines. It draws on like an electron beam, pulses with the beat and shatters into segments.
- **Techniques:** 3D vector geometry with per-line depth of field, 2D HUD and kinetic typography, a GPU fluid simulation (nebula and smoke), particles (hat sparks, speed streaks, shattered letters), shockwave refraction, chromatic aberration, zoom blur, anamorphic streaks, bloom, iris masking between scenes, and focus pulls.

## Audio -> visual mapping
| Audio feature | Visual response |
|---|---|
| **Kick** | A reticle gate travels down the highway and crosses the strike reticle on the kick's frame, then explodes outward. Also: a shockwave refraction ring, camera shake scaled by sub, a strike-reticle flash, a scale punch on the core/sun, a radial fluid burst, a terrain ripple, +100 score |
| **Snare / clap** | Bright wall panel arrival and flash, icosahedron faces light up, a ring of fluid splats, a small exposure surge |
| **Hi-hat** | Wall sparks with particle bursts, star twinkle, tick marks brighten, orbit particles lit in sequence, and in the intro one title letter typed per hat |
| **Beat / downbeat** | Every beat ring on the 16th grid flares at the strike plane; HUD beat lamps (the downbeat lamp is larger); intro reticle, gyroscope and radar rings pulse on every beat, harder on downbeats |
| **Phrase (4/8/16 bars)** | Camera roll or orbit-angle cut, chorus heading change, palette hue notch, one extra tunnel layer per phrase in drop 1 |
| **Sub / bass** | Tunnel radius and pressure, terrain height and kick ripple, FOV breathing, camera shake depth, core scale |
| **Mids / lead** | Two bar-locked fluid emitters (one orbit per 4 beats), hue drift from pitch class and spectral centroid, title stroke weight, sun glow |
| **Highs** | Speed-streak density, star twinkle, tick sparkle; in the breakdown the lens defocuses as the high band is filtered away and refocuses as it returns |
| **Loudness** | Exposure, travel speed (`activity`), motion amplitude; near-silence at the start and end means stillness |
| **Future spectrum** | Each tunnel ring and terrain row is shaped by the spectrum at the moment it will reach the camera, so the music ahead is visible |

## Section treatments
| Section | Treatment |
|---|---|
| Intro | A single pip in silence; the reticle draws on over 4 bars, hats add ticks, sub swells send pressure rings; ARCADE RUSH types on letter by letter from the first phrase at 8 s or later, VOHO appears on the next phrase |
| Build (x3) | The highway accelerates (speed rises with progress squared, sync stays exact), FOV tightens, reticle ticks double every bar, a bar countdown (3-2-1 / 4-3-2-1 / 2-1), rising zoom blur and chromatic aberration, a warming grade, suction on the final beat. Build 2 tilts down from the radar map into the tunnel |
| Drop (x3) | The rhythm-highway tunnel. "RUSH" slams on the first beat and shatters on the next downbeat, becoming "RUSH x2" and "RUSH x3". Drop 2 starts fully layered with ember accents and a faster speed; drop 3 adds the terrain canyon and white-hot accents |
| Chorus (x2) | A spectrogram mountain terrain along a road, the reticle sun with a spectrum ring, ARCADE / RUSH words arriving on downbeats, a teal fluid sky. Chorus 2 adds a mirrored ceiling (canyon), magenta accents and a faster speed |
| Verse | The gyroscope core: reticle rings rotating at 4 / 2 / -4 beats per revolution, a snare-lit icosahedron, an equatorial spectrum, hat-lit orbit particles; the camera cuts to a new orbit angle every phrase; the dim highway continues behind |
| Bridge | A shift in perspective, palette and scale: a top-down amber radar where the sweep turns once per bar and every onset is a blip at its bar position (hit by the sweep exactly as it sounds); the camera rises to reveal the scale |
| Breakdown | Tunnel with focus tied to the high band: defocused and desaturated while the filter is closed, snapping back into focus as it opens |
| Outro | The world winds down with the final chord; the lockup (reticle + ARCADE RUSH + VOHO) draws on and holds as the clean final frame |

## Visual identity
Derived from the cover art (a retro sci-fi cockpit with green holographic HUD rings and amber instrument lights) and the track (a 108 BPM four-on-the-floor synth instrumental).
- **Palette:** teal-black void; phosphor green (primary lines); amber (instruments, downbeats, type); cyan for highs and sparks; ember and magenta held back for escalation (drop 2+, chorus 2); white-hot for impacts.
- **Motif:** the **targeting reticle** (rings, ticks, crosshair gaps, centre pip). It is the HUD, every kick gate in the tunnel, the horizon sun, the gyroscope core, the radar, and the final lockup.
- **Type:** a custom chamfered stroke font drawn as glowing vector lines. It draws on like an electron beam, pulses with the beat and shatters into segments.
- **Techniques:** 3D vector geometry with per-line depth of field, 2D HUD and kinetic typography, a GPU fluid simulation (nebula and smoke), particles (hat sparks, speed streaks, shattered letters), shockwave refraction, chromatic aberration, zoom blur, anamorphic streaks, bloom, iris masking between scenes, and focus pulls.

## Audio -> visual mapping
| Audio feature | Visual response |
|---|---|
| **Kick** | A reticle gate travels down the highway and crosses the strike reticle on the kick's frame, then explodes outward. Also: a shockwave refraction ring, camera shake scaled by sub, a strike-reticle flash, a scale punch on the core/sun, a radial fluid burst, a terrain ripple, +100 score |
| **Snare / clap** | Bright wall panel arrival and flash, icosahedron faces light up, a ring of fluid splats, a small exposure surge |
| **Hi-hat** | Wall sparks with particle bursts, star twinkle, tick marks brighten, orbit particles lit in sequence, and in the intro one title letter typed per hat |
| **Beat / downbeat** | Every beat ring on the 16th grid flares at the strike plane; HUD beat lamps (the downbeat lamp is larger); intro reticle, gyroscope and radar rings pulse on every beat, harder on downbeats |
| **Phrase (4/8/16 bars)** | Camera roll or orbit-angle cut, chorus heading change, palette hue notch, one extra tunnel layer per phrase in drop 1 |
| **Sub / bass** | Tunnel radius and pressure, terrain height and kick ripple, FOV breathing, camera shake depth, core scale |
| **Mids / lead** | Two bar-locked fluid emitters (one orbit per 4 beats), hue drift from pitch class and spectral centroid, title stroke weight, sun glow |
| **Highs** | Speed-streak density, star twinkle, tick sparkle; in the breakdown the lens defocuses as the high band is filtered away and refocuses as it returns |
| **Loudness** | Exposure, travel speed (`activity`), motion amplitude; near-silence at the start and end means stillness |
| **Future spectrum** | Each tunnel ring and terrain row is shaped by the spectrum at the moment it will reach the camera, so the music ahead is visible |

## Section treatments
| Section | Treatment |
|---|---|
| Intro | A single pip in silence; the reticle draws on over 4 bars, hats add ticks, sub swells send pressure rings; ARCADE RUSH types on letter by letter from the first phrase at 8 s or later, VOHO appears on the next phrase |
| Build (x3) | The highway accelerates (speed rises with progress squared, sync stays exact), FOV tightens, reticle ticks double every bar, a bar countdown (3-2-1 / 4-3-2-1 / 2-1), rising zoom blur and chromatic aberration, a warming grade, suction on the final beat. Build 2 tilts down from the radar map into the tunnel |
| Drop (x3) | The rhythm-highway tunnel. "RUSH" slams on the first beat and shatters on the next downbeat, becoming "RUSH x2" and "RUSH x3". Drop 2 starts fully layered with ember accents and a faster speed; drop 3 adds the terrain canyon and white-hot accents |
| Chorus (x2) | A spectrogram mountain terrain along a road, the reticle sun with a spectrum ring, ARCADE / RUSH words arriving on downbeats, a teal fluid sky. Chorus 2 adds a mirrored ceiling (canyon), magenta accents and a faster speed |
| Verse | The gyroscope core: reticle rings rotating at 4 / 2 / -4 beats per revolution, a snare-lit icosahedron, an equatorial spectrum, hat-lit orbit particles; the camera cuts to a new orbit angle every phrase; the dim highway continues behind |
| Bridge | A shift in perspective, palette and scale: a top-down amber radar where the sweep turns once per bar and every onset is a blip at its bar position (hit by the sweep exactly as it sounds); the camera rises to reveal the scale |
| Breakdown | Tunnel with focus tied to the high band: defocused and desaturated while the filter is closed, snapping back into focus as it opens |
| Outro | The world winds down with the final chord; the lockup (reticle + ARCADE RUSH + VOHO) draws on and holds as the clean final frame |

# Engine and signal-layer reference

## timeline.Timeline(path) — per-frame arrays (length n = frames)
- clocks: `t`, `beatpos` (continuous beat index), `barpos`, `beat_frac`, `bpm`, `beat_period`, `flow` (beat time x activity)
- bands: `bands[k]` raw, `s[k]` fast-attack/slow-release, `s_slow[k]` (k in sub, bass, lowmid, highmid, high, loud, lead, centroid, flux); `spec32`, `spec_s` (smoothed); `pitch_class`; `activity` (loudness gated by silence = master motion amplitude)
- envelopes (instant attack on nearest frame, exp decay): `kick` (tau 0.16), `kick_fast` (0.07), `snare`, `hat`, `other`, `beat`, `down`, `impact`, `sec_change`, `phrase` (level-weighted)
- since/index: `kick_since`, `kick_idx`, `snare_*`, `hat_*`, `beat_since`, `down_*`, `phrase_since`, `phrase_idx`, `phrase_level`, `sec_since`
- sections: `sec_idx`, `sec_time`, `sec_left`, `sec_prog`, `sections` (raw dicts), `section(f)`
- onsets: `on[k] = (times, strengths)`; `beat_t`, `beat_down`, `beat_bar`, `beat_inbar`
- arcade counters: `score` (kick 100 / snare 50 / hat 10, cumulative), `combo` (consecutive beats that had a kick)
- helpers: `envelope(times, strengths, tau)`, `since(times)`, `frame_of(times)`, `spec_at(times)`

## gfx
- `Camera(eye, target, up, fov, roll, focus, aperture, near, far)`. `aperture` > 0 gives line depth of field (CoC px = aperture * f_px * |1/z - 1/focus|, capped by `maxcoc`).
- `Lines()`: `.add(a[N,3], b[N,3], color[N,3] or [3], wpx, wworld)`, `.polyline(pts, color, wpx, closed)`. Colors are linear HDR (values > 1 bloom). Width = pixels + world units (perspective).
- `circle_pts(center, r, n, u, v, a0, a1, radii)`, `rot(axis, angle)`, `look_at`, `perspective`.
- `Fluid(ctx, sim, dye)`: `.splat(x, y, vx, vy, rgb, radius)` (uv, y up; velocity in sim texels/s), `.step(curl, vel_diss, dye_diss, iters)`, `.dye_tex`. Stateful: render sequentially, or warm up (render.py does `--warmup` seconds of `scene.fluid(f)`).
- `Engine(W, H)`:
  - `begin(slot, bg, cam)` clears scene slot 0/1 and draws the sky: `sky_top, sky_bot, horizon, horizon_w, up, star_amt, star_twinkle, star_seed, neb_amt` (fluid dye as nebula), `neb_shift, neb_mask_sky` (1 = only above the horizon), `fogcol, fogamt`
  - `draw(lines, cam, fog=, gain=, maxcoc=)` additive capsules with DOF into the current slot. `draw(lines, None, hud=True)` goes to the HUD layer (pixel coordinates, origin at the centre, y up, z = -1)
  - `clear_hud()` once per frame before HUD draws
  - `finish(post)` composites slots (iris mask), bloom (6 mips), anamorphic streak, final pass. The HUD is bloomed but never distorted
  - `read()` returns RGB24 bytes, top row first
- post keys (defaults in `DEFAULT_POST`): `bloom_amt, bloom_threshold, bloom_knee, streak_amt, streak_tint, exposure, flash, flash_col, ca, barrel, zoomblur, center, shocks=[(x,y,radius,strength) x <= 4], kaleido, kaleido_n, kaleido_rot, defocus, saturation, lift, gain, contrast, vignette, scan, grain, fade, tint, tint_amt, mix_mode, iris_c, iris_r, edge_col, xfade, hud_gain`

## vfont
`text_segments(s, size, tracking, align)` returns `([(i, ch, segs(N,2,2), cx)], width)`; `draw_on(segs, p)`; glyphs A-Z, 0-9, `- . : / ! ? + x > < [ ] # '` and space (lowercase maps to uppercase; `x` is the multiplication sign).

## render.py CLI
`--workdir --scene [--out] [--start --end] [--stills t1,t2] [--debug] [--warmup 4] [--crf 18] [--preset slow] [--width --height]`

## Performance (M1 Max, 1080p60)
Engine init 0.2 s. A simple scene takes 11 ms per frame. The full Arcade Rush scene (20-40k segments, fluid 320x180 / 960x540 with 22 Jacobi iterations, 2 scene slots during transitions) runs at 20-28 fps including libx264 `slow`. Numpy geometry is the main CPU cost; keep it vectorised (one `.add` per layer, never per segment in Python loops when N > ~50).

## Gotchas already hit (and fixes)
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| GL context: "cannot choose pixel format" | sandbox blocks the GPU | run render commands with the sandbox disabled |
| White blob at the vanishing point / horizon band | additive lines pile up where far geometry converges | fog 0.006+, FAR <= 380, per-row `exp(-d/110..140)` fade, dimmer far gates |
| Whole frame turns beige on drops | additive flash lifts blacks massively after ACES + sRGB | exposure surge `exposure *= 1 + 0.9*surge`, additive flash <= 0.012 |
| HUD text mangled by zoom blur / kaleidoscope | HUD in the distorted scene | draw HUD with `hud=True` (own layer) |
| Ghost copies of HUD text | kaleidoscope folds the bloom (which includes the HUD) | avoid kaleido while big HUD text is up, or skip kaleido |
| Starfield like snow | too many stars | threshold 0.955, sharp falloff (already set) |
| Kick flash one frame before the section cut | grid beat vs kick straddle a frame | beats snapped to kicks in analyze.py (already done) |
| Muddy smoke everywhere | fluid dye too strong | kick dye ~0.045*s, lead ~0.012, `dye_diss` 0.9-1.7, `neb_amt` 0.45-0.9 |
| Mountains off-screen, flat ground | terrain too wide for the FOV | columns within +-70 units, camera at y 4-5 looking slightly down |
| One-frame section "slivers" | segmentation leftovers | handled in analyze (min lengths); re-inspect after tuning |
| 3 flashes/s at the build->drop hand-off | countdown beat pulses + suction dip + drop surge stack up within 1 s | beat pulse <= 0.7, suction <= 0.2, surge <= 0.6 (verify reports the worst window) |
| 3 flashes/s during snare rolls | snare-driven bloom on a big central object | keep snare gain on large bright shapes ~1x, push the accent into small elements |
| Beats "without a visible hit" in sparse sections | only the tiny HUD lamps react | add a small per-beat pulse to a large element (ring width/brightness) in intro/bridge |
| A/V end window reports tens of ms | waveform correlation on a sustained decaying chord is ambiguous | verify anchors windows on kicks (fixed); spot-check with a transient window if in doubt |

# Engine and signal-layer reference

## timeline.Timeline(path) — per-frame arrays (length n = frames)
- clocks: `t`, `beatpos` (continuous beat index), `barpos`, `beat_frac`, `bpm`, `beat_period`, `flow` (beat time x activity)
- bands: `bands[k]` raw, `s[k]` fast-attack/slow-release, `s_slow[k]` (k in sub, bass, lowmid, highmid, high, loud, lead, centroid, flux); `spec32`, `spec_s` (smoothed); `pitch_class`; `activity` (loudness gated by silence = master motion amplitude)
- envelopes (instant attack on nearest frame, exp decay): `kick` (tau 0.16), `kick_fast` (0.07), `snare`, `hat`, `other`, `beat`, `down`, `impact`, `sec_change`, `phrase` (level-weighted)
- since/index: `kick_since`, `kick_idx`, `snare_*`, `hat_*`, `beat_since`, `down_*`, `phrase_since`, `phrase_idx`, `phrase_level`, `sec_since`
- sections: `sec_idx`, `sec_time`, `sec_left`, `sec_prog`, `sections` (raw dicts), `section(f)`
- onsets: `on[k] = (times, strengths)`; `beat_t`, `beat_down`, `beat_bar`, `beat_inbar`
- arcade counters: `score` (kick 100 / snare 50 / hat 10, cumulative), `combo` (consecutive beats that had a kick)
- helpers: `envelope(times, strengths, tau)`, `since(times)`, `frame_of(times)`, `spec_at(times)`

## gfx
- `Camera(eye, target, up, fov, roll, focus, aperture, near, far)`. `aperture` > 0 gives line depth of field (CoC px = aperture * f_px * |1/z - 1/focus|, capped by `maxcoc`).
- `Lines()`: `.add(a[N,3], b[N,3], color[N,3] or [3], wpx, wworld)`, `.polyline(pts, color, wpx, closed)`. Colors are linear HDR (values > 1 bloom). Width = pixels + world units (perspective).
- `circle_pts(center, r, n, u, v, a0, a1, radii)`, `rot(axis, angle)`, `look_at`, `perspective`.
- `Fluid(ctx, sim, dye)`: `.splat(x, y, vx, vy, rgb, radius)` (uv, y up; velocity in sim texels/s), `.step(curl, vel_diss, dye_diss, iters)`, `.dye_tex`. Stateful: render sequentially, or warm up (render.py does `--warmup` seconds of `scene.fluid(f)`).
- `Engine(W, H)`:
  - `begin(slot, bg, cam)` clears scene slot 0/1 and draws the sky: `sky_top, sky_bot, horizon, horizon_w, up, star_amt, star_twinkle, star_seed, neb_amt` (fluid dye as nebula), `neb_shift, neb_mask_sky` (1 = only above the horizon), `fogcol, fogamt`
  - `draw(lines, cam, fog=, gain=, maxcoc=)` additive capsules with DOF into the current slot. `draw(lines, None, hud=True)` goes to the HUD layer (pixel coordinates, origin at the centre, y up, z = -1)
  - `clear_hud()` once per frame before HUD draws
  - `finish(post)` composites slots (iris mask), bloom (6 mips), anamorphic streak, final pass. The HUD is bloomed but never distorted
  - `read()` returns RGB24 bytes, top row first
- post keys (defaults in `DEFAULT_POST`): `bloom_amt, bloom_threshold, bloom_knee, streak_amt, streak_tint, exposure, flash, flash_col, ca, barrel, zoomblur, center, shocks=[(x,y,radius,strength) x <= 4], kaleido, kaleido_n, kaleido_rot, defocus, saturation, lift, gain, contrast, vignette, scan, grain, fade, tint, tint_amt, mix_mode, iris_c, iris_r, edge_col, xfade, hud_gain`

## vfont
`text_segments(s, size, tracking, align)` returns `([(i, ch, segs(N,2,2), cx)], width)`; `draw_on(segs, p)`; glyphs A-Z, 0-9, `- . : / ! ? + x > < [ ] # '` and space (lowercase maps to uppercase; `x` is the multiplication sign).

## render.py CLI
`--workdir --scene [--out] [--start --end] [--stills t1,t2] [--debug] [--warmup 4] [--crf 18] [--preset slow] [--width --height]`

## Performance (M1 Max, 1080p60)
Engine init 0.2 s. A simple scene takes 11 ms per frame. The full Arcade Rush scene (20-40k segments, fluid 320x180 / 960x540 with 22 Jacobi iterations, 2 scene slots during transitions) runs at 20-28 fps including libx264 `slow`. Numpy geometry is the main CPU cost; keep it vectorised (one `.add` per layer, never per segment in Python loops when N > ~50).

## Gotchas already hit (and fixes)
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| GL context: "cannot choose pixel format" | sandbox blocks the GPU | run render commands with the sandbox disabled |
| White blob at the vanishing point / horizon band | additive lines pile up where far geometry converges | fog 0.006+, FAR <= 380, per-row `exp(-d/110..140)` fade, dimmer far gates |
| Whole frame turns beige on drops | additive flash lifts blacks massively after ACES + sRGB | exposure surge `exposure *= 1 + 0.9*surge`, additive flash <= 0.012 |
| HUD text mangled by zoom blur / kaleidoscope | HUD in the distorted scene | draw HUD with `hud=True` (own layer) |
| Ghost copies of HUD text | kaleidoscope folds the bloom (which includes the HUD) | avoid kaleido while big HUD text is up, or skip kaleido |
| Starfield like snow | too many stars | threshold 0.955, sharp falloff (already set) |
| Kick flash one frame before the section cut | grid beat vs kick straddle a frame | beats snapped to kicks in analyze.py (already done) |
| Muddy smoke everywhere | fluid dye too strong | kick dye ~0.045*s, lead ~0.012, `dye_diss` 0.9-1.7, `neb_amt` 0.45-0.9 |
| Mountains off-screen, flat ground | terrain too wide for the FOV | columns within +-70 units, camera at y 4-5 looking slightly down |
| One-frame section "slivers" | segmentation leftovers | handled in analyze (min lengths); re-inspect after tuning |
| 3 flashes/s at the build->drop hand-off | countdown beat pulses + suction dip + drop surge stack up within 1 s | beat pulse <= 0.7, suction <= 0.2, surge <= 0.6 (verify reports the worst window) |
| 3 flashes/s during snare rolls | snare-driven bloom on a big central object | keep snare gain on large bright shapes ~1x, push the accent into small elements |
| Beats "without a visible hit" in sparse sections | only the tiny HUD lamps react | add a small per-beat pulse to a large element (ring width/brightness) in intro/bridge |
| A/V end window reports tens of ms | waveform correlation on a sustained decaying chord is ambiguous | verify anchors windows on kicks (fixed); spot-check with a transient window if in doubt |

"""Signal layer: turns timeline.json into per-frame control signals.

Everything the renderer animates is read from here. Rules:
  * event envelopes jump to full value on the frame nearest the transient (never later), then decay
  * continuous band signals use fast attack / slow release one-pole smoothing (no added lag on rises)
  * cyclic motion uses `beatpos` (continuous beat index) so it is phase-locked to the grid
  * non-cyclic drift uses `flow`: beat time weighted by loudness, so silence means stillness
"""
import json
import numpy as np


def _smooth_ar(x, att, rel):
    y = np.empty_like(x)
    acc = x[0]
    for i, v in enumerate(x):
        acc += (v - acc) * (att if v > acc else rel)
        y[i] = acc
    return y


class Timeline:
    def __init__(self, path='timeline.json'):
        T = json.load(open(path))
        self.raw = T
        m = T['meta']
        self.fps = m['fps']
        self.n = m['n_frames']
        self.duration = m['duration']
        self.title, self.artist = m['title'], m['artist']
        fps, n = self.fps, self.n
        self.t = np.arange(n) / fps
        t = self.t

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- beat grid clocks

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- arcade counters (onset integrals)
        kt, ks = self.on['kick']
        score_ev = np.concatenate([kt, self.on['snare'][0], self.on['hat'][0]])
        score_val = np.concatenate([np.full(len(kt), 100), np.full(len(self.on['snare'][0]), 50), np.full(len(self.on['hat'][0]), 10)])
        o = np.argsort(score_ev)
        score_ev, score_val = score_ev[o], score_val[o]
        ev_frame = np.round(score_ev * fps).astype(int)
        cs = np.cumsum(score_val)
        k = np.searchsorted(ev_frame, np.arange(n), side='right')
        self.score = np.where(k > 0, cs[np.clip(k - 1, 0, len(cs) - 1)], 0)
        # combo: consecutive beats that carried a kick; resets on a beat without one
        has_kick = np.array([np.any(np.abs(kt - b) < 0.05) for b in bt])
        combo_b = np.zeros(len(bt), int)
        c = 0
        for i, hk in enumerate(has_kick):
            c = c + 1 if hk else 0
            combo_b[i] = c
        bi = np.clip(np.searchsorted(np.round(bt * fps), np.arange(n), side='right') - 1, 0, len(bt) - 1)
        self.combo = np.where(t >= bt[0] - 0.5 / fps, combo_b[bi], 0)

        # travel distance for highway mapping (per section speed profiles are applied in scenes)
        self.frame_of = lambda tt: np.clip(np.round(np.asarray(tt) * fps).astype(int), 0, n - 1)

    def _smooth_spec(self):
        out = np.empty_like(self.spec32)
        acc = self.spec32[0].copy()
        for i in range(len(self.spec32)):
            v = self.spec32[i]
            acc += (v - acc) * np.where(v > acc, 0.7, 0.12)
            out[i] = acc
        return out

    def envelope(self, times, strength, tau):
        """Jump to strength on the frame nearest the event, exponential decay afterwards."""
        n, fps = self.n, self.fps
        y = np.zeros(n, np.float32)
        if len(times) == 0:
            return y
        fr = np.round(np.asarray(times) * fps).astype(int)
        imp = np.zeros(n)
        tev = np.full(n, -1.0)
        for f, s, te in zip(fr, strength, times):
            if 0 <= f < n and s >= imp[f]:
                imp[f] = s
                tev[f] = te
        acc = 0.0
        dec = np.exp(-1.0 / (fps * tau))
        for i in range(n):
            acc *= dec
            if imp[i] > 0:
                # value at this frame measured from the true event time (never below full on its own frame)
                acc = max(acc, imp[i] * min(1.0, np.exp(-max(0.0, self.t[i] - tev[i]) / tau)))
            y[i] = acc
        return y

    def since(self, times):
        """Seconds since the last event whose nearest frame has been reached, and its index (-1 before first)."""
        fr = np.round(np.asarray(times) * self.fps).astype(int)
        k = np.searchsorted(fr, np.arange(self.n), side='right') - 1
        ts = np.where(k >= 0, self.t - np.asarray(times)[np.clip(k, 0, max(0, len(fr) - 1))], 99.0)
        return np.maximum(ts, 0.0), k

    # convenience for scenes -------------------------------------------------
    def section(self, f):
        return self.sections[self.sec_idx[f]]

    def spec_at(self, times):
        f = self.frame_of(times)
        return self.spec32[f]

    def band_at(self, name, times):
        return self.bands[name][self.frame_of(times)]


if __name__ == '__main__':
    import time
    t0 = time.time()
    tl = Timeline()
    print(f'loaded in {time.time()-t0:.1f}s; frames {tl.n}; beats {len(tl.beat_t)}')
    for f in [0, 150, 2412, 4413, 8680, 11747, 12285]:
        s = tl.section(f)
        print(f, f'{tl.t[f]:.2f}s', s['label'], s['occurrence'], f'beatpos {tl.beatpos[f]:.2f} bar {tl.barpos[f]:.2f}',
              f'kick {tl.kick[f]:.2f} act {tl.activity[f]:.2f} flow {tl.flow[f]:.1f} score {tl.score[f]} combo {tl.combo[f]}')

    """'03_night-blur (master v2).wav' -> ('Night Blur', None); 'voho - Bad Boys.wav' -> ('Bad Boys', 'voho')."""
    stem = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(path))[0]
    stem = re.sub(r'[_]+', ' ', stem)
    stem = re.sub(r'[\(\[][^\)\]]*(master|mix|final|v\d+|bounce|export|wav|24bit|16bit)[^\)\]]*[\)\]]', '', stem, flags=re.I)
    stem = re.sub(r'\b(final|master(ed)?|bounce|export|v\d+)\b', '', stem, flags=re.I)
    stem = re.sub(r'^\s*\d{1,3}\s*[-.\s]\s*', '', stem)              # leading track number
    artist = None
    if ' - ' in stem:

    stem = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', stem).strip(' -.')
    if stem and (stem.islower() or stem.isupper()):
        stem = stem.title()
    return stem or os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(path))[0], artist

self.phrase_since, self.phrase_idx = self.since(pt)
        self.phrase_level = np.where(self.phrase_idx >= 0, pl[np.clip(self.phrase_idx, 0, len(pl) - 1)], 0)

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- arcade counters (onset integrals)
        kt, ks = self.on['kick']
        score_ev = np.concatenate([kt, self.on['snare'][0], self.on['hat'][0]])
        score_val = np.concatenate([np.full(len(kt), 100), np.full(len(self.on['snare'][0]), 50), np.full(len(self.on['hat'][0]), 10)])
        o = np.argsort(score_ev)
        score_ev, score_val = score_ev[o], score_val[o]
        ev_frame = np.round(score_ev * fps).astype(int)
        cs = np.cumsum(score_val)
        k = np.searchsorted(ev_frame, np.arange(n), side='right')
        self.score = np.where(k > 0, cs[np.clip(k - 1, 0, len(cs) - 1)], 0)
        # combo: consecutive beats that carried a kick; resets on a beat without one
        has_kick = np.array([np.any(np.abs(kt - b) < 0.05) for b in bt])
        combo_b = np.zeros(len(bt), int)
        c = 0
        for i, hk in enumerate(has_kick):
            c = c + 1 if hk else 0
            combo_b[i] = c
        bi = np.clip(np.searchsorted(np.round(bt * fps), np.arange(n), side='right') - 1, 0, len(bt) - 1)
        self.combo = np.where(t >= bt[0] - 0.5 / fps, combo_b[bi], 0)

        # travel distance for highway mapping (per section speed profiles are applied in scenes)
        self.frame_of = lambda tt: np.clip(np.round(np.asarray(tt) * fps).astype(int), 0, n - 1)

        \"\"\"Raw waveform window for frame f, for oscilloscope-style visuals (48 kHz, float, roughly -1..1).

        Returns (n,) mono, or (n, 2) L/R when stereo=True (use L vs R for an XY / Lissajous scope).
        The window is centred on the frame time. trigger=True shifts it (by at most n/4) to the nearest rising

            seg = self._trig[lo - 1:hi]
            zc = np.nonzero((seg[:-1] < 0) & (seg[1:] >= 0))[0] + lo
            if len(zc):

        idx = np.clip(np.arange(s0, s0 + n), 0, len(x) - 1)
        w = x[idx]

"""Signal layer: turns timeline.json into per-frame control signals.

Everything the renderer animates is read from here. Rules:
  * event envelopes jump to full value on the frame nearest the transient (never later), then decay
  * continuous band signals use fast attack / slow release one-pole smoothing (no added lag on rises)
  * cyclic motion uses `beatpos` (continuous beat index) so it is phase-locked to the grid
  * non-cyclic drift uses `flow`: beat time weighted by loudness, so silence means stillness
"""
import json
import numpy as np


def _smooth_ar(x, att, rel):
    y = np.empty_like(x)
    acc = x[0]
    for i, v in enumerate(x):
        acc += (v - acc) * (att if v > acc else rel)
        y[i] = acc
    return y


class Timeline:
    def __init__(self, path='timeline.json'):
        T = json.load(open(path))
        self.raw = T
        m = T['meta']
        self.fps = m['fps']
        self.n = m['n_frames']
        self.duration = m['duration']
        self.title, self.artist = m['title'], m['artist']
        fps, n = self.fps, self.n
        self.t = np.arange(n) / fps
        t = self.t

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- beat grid clocks
        bt = np.array([b['t'] for b in T['beats']])
        self.beat_t = bt
        self.beat_down = np.array([b['downbeat'] for b in T['beats']])
        self.beat_bar = np.array([b['bar'] for b in T['beats']])
        self.beat_inbar = np.array([b['beat'] for b in T['beats']])
        idx = np.arange(len(bt), dtype=float)
        p0, p1 = bt[1] - bt[0], bt[-1] - bt[-2]
        bp = np.interp(t, bt, idx)
        bp = np.where(t < bt[0], (t - bt[0]) / p0, bp)
        bp = np.where(t > bt[-1], len(bt) - 1 + (t - bt[-1]) / p1, bp)
        self.beatpos = bp                                   # continuous beat index
        first_down = int(np.argmax(self.beat_down))
        self.barpos = (bp - first_down) / 4.0 + self.beat_bar[first_down]   # continuous bar index
        self.beat_frac = bp - np.floor(bp)
        self.bpm = 60.0 / np.interp(t, bt[1:], np.diff(bt), left=p0, right=p1)
        self.beat_period = 60.0 / self.bpm

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- per-frame bands
        F = T['frames']
        self.bands = {k: np.array(F[k], dtype=np.float32) for k in ['sub', 'bass', 'lowmid', 'highmid', 'high', 'loud', 'lead', 'centroid', 'flux']}
        self.silent = np.array(F['silent'], dtype=np.float32)
        self.pitch_class = np.array(F['pitch_class'])
        self.spec32 = np.array(T['spectrum32'], dtype=np.float32)
        att, rel = 0.65, 0.09
        self.s = {k: _smooth_ar(v, att, rel) for k, v in self.bands.items()}
        self.s_slow = {k: _smooth_ar(v, 0.08, 0.02) for k, v in self.bands.items()}
        # overall activity: loudness gated by absolute silence -> motion amplitude master
        self.activity = np.clip(_smooth_ar(self.bands['loud'] * (1 - self.silent), 0.5, 0.05), 0, 1)
        dbeat = np.r_[0, np.diff(bp)]
        self.flow = np.cumsum(dbeat * (0.15 + 0.85 * self.activity))        # energy-weighted beat time
        self.spec_s = self._smooth_spec()

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- onsets
        O = T['onsets']
        self.on = {k: (np.array(v['t']), np.array(v['s'])) for k, v in O.items()}
        self.kick = self.envelope(*self.on['kick'], tau=0.16)
        self.kick_fast = self.envelope(*self.on['kick'], tau=0.07)
        self.snare = self.envelope(*self.on['snare'], tau=0.12)
        self.hat = self.envelope(*self.on['hat'], tau=0.06)
        self.other = self.envelope(*self.on['other'], tau=0.18)
        self.beat = self.envelope(bt, np.ones(len(bt)), tau=0.14)
        self.down = self.envelope(bt[self.beat_down], np.ones(self.beat_down.sum()), tau=0.35)
        imp = T['impacts']
        self.impact = self.envelope(np.array([i['t'] for i in imp]), np.clip(np.array([i['db'] for i in imp]) / 30, 0.4, 1), tau=0.5)

        self.snare_since, self.snare_idx = self.since(self.on['snare'][0])
        self.hat_since, self.hat_idx = self.since(self.on['hat'][0])
        self.beat_since, _ = self.since(bt)
        self.down_since, self.down_idx = self.since(bt[self.beat_down])

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- sections & phrases
        S = T['sections']
        self.sections = S
        st = np.array([s['start'] for s in S])
        self.sec_idx = np.clip(np.searchsorted(st, t + 0.5 / fps, side='right') - 1, 0, len(S) - 1)
        s0 = st[self.sec_idx]
        s1 = np.array([S[i]['end'] for i in self.sec_idx])
        self.sec_time = t - s0
        self.sec_left = s1 - t
        self.sec_prog = np.clip((t - s0) / (s1 - s0), 0, 1)
        # section progress measured in bars (for countdowns / phrase logic)
        self.sec_bar0 = np.array([S[i]['bar0'] for i in self.sec_idx])
        self.sec_bars = np.array([S[i]['bar1'] - S[i]['bar0'] for i in self.sec_idx])
        self.sec_change = self.envelope(st[1:], np.ones(len(st) - 1), tau=0.6)
        self.sec_since, _ = self.since(st[1:])

        pt = np.array([p['t'] for p in P])
        pl = np.array([p['level'] for p in P])

        self.phrase_level = np.where(self.phrase_idx >= 0, pl[np.clip(self.phrase_idx, 0, len(pl) - 1)], 0)

        kt, ks = self.on['kick']
        score_ev = np.concatenate([kt, self.on['snare'][0], self.on['hat'][0]])
        score_val = np.concatenate([np.full(len(kt), 100), np.full(len(self.on['snare'][0]), 50), np.full(len(self.on['hat'][0]), 10)])
        o = np.argsort(score_ev)
        score_ev, score_val = score_ev[o], score_val[o]
        ev_frame = np.round(score_ev * fps).astype(int)
        cs = np.cumsum(score_val)
        k = np.searchsorted(ev_frame, np.arange(n), side='right')
        self.score = np.where(k > 0, cs[np.clip(k - 1, 0, len(cs) - 1)], 0)
        # combo: consecutive beats that carried a kick; resets on a beat without one
        has_kick = np.array([np.any(np.abs(kt - b) < 0.05) for b in bt])
        combo_b = np.zeros(len(bt), int)
        c = 0

        acc = self.spec32[0].copy()
        for i in range(len(self.spec32)):
            v = self.spec32[i]
            acc += (v - acc) * np.where(v > acc, 0.7, 0.12)
            out[i] = acc
        return out

    def envelope(self, times, strength, tau):
        """Jump to strength on the frame nearest the event, exponential decay afterwards."""
        n, fps = self.n, self.fps
        y = np.zeros(n, np.float32)
        if len(times) == 0:
            return y
        fr = np.round(np.asarray(times) * fps).astype(int)
        imp = np.zeros(n)
        tev = np.full(n, -1.0)
        for f, s, te in zip(fr, strength, times):
            if 0 <= f < n and s >= imp[f]:
                imp[f] = s
                tev[f] = te
        acc = 0.0
        dec = np.exp(-1.0 / (fps * tau))
        for i in range(n):
            acc *= dec
            if imp[i] > 0:
                # value at this frame measured from the true event time (never below full on its own frame)
                acc = max(acc, imp[i] * min(1.0, np.exp(-max(0.0, self.t[i] - tev[i]) / tau)))
            y[i] = acc
        return y

    def since(self, times):
        """Seconds since the last event whose nearest frame has been reached, and its index (-1 before first)."""
        fr = np.round(np.asarray(times) * self.fps).astype(int)
        k = np.searchsorted(fr, np.arange(self.n), side='right') - 1
        ts = np.where(k >= 0, self.t - np.asarray(times)[np.clip(k, 0, max(0, len(fr) - 1))], 99.0)

    def section(self, f):
        return self.sections[self.sec_idx[f]]

    def spec_at(self, times):
        f = self.frame_of(times)
        return self.spec32[f]

    def band_at(self, name, times):
        return self.bands[name][self.frame_of(times)]

        """Raw waveform window for frame f, for oscilloscope-style visuals (48 kHz float, roughly -1..1).

"""Signal layer: turns timeline.json into per-frame control signals.

Everything the renderer animates is read from here. Rules:
  * event envelopes jump to full value on the frame nearest the transient (never later), then decay
  * continuous band signals use fast attack / slow release one-pole smoothing (no added lag on rises)
  * cyclic motion uses `beatpos` (continuous beat index) so it is phase-locked to the grid
  * non-cyclic drift uses `flow`: beat time weighted by loudness, so silence means stillness
"""
import json
import os
import numpy as np


def _smooth_ar(x, att, rel):
    y = np.empty_like(x)
    acc = x[0]
    for i, v in enumerate(x):
        acc += (v - acc) * (att if v > acc else rel)
        y[i] = acc
    return y


class Timeline:
    def __init__(self, path='timeline.json'):
        T = json.load(open(path))
        self.raw = T
        self.audio_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), 'audio.wav')
        self._pcm = None
        m = T['meta']
        self.fps = m['fps']
        self.n = m['n_frames']
        self.duration = m['duration']
        self.title, self.artist = m['title'], m['artist']
        fps, n = self.fps, self.n
        self.t = np.arange(n) / fps
        t = self.t

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- beat grid clocks
        bt = np.array([b['t'] for b in T['beats']])
        self.beat_t = bt
        self.beat_down = np.array([b['downbeat'] for b in T['beats']])
        self.beat_bar = np.array([b['bar'] for b in T['beats']])
        self.beat_inbar = np.array([b['beat'] for b in T['beats']])
        idx = np.arange(len(bt), dtype=float)
        p0, p1 = bt[1] - bt[0], bt[-1] - bt[-2]
        bp = np.interp(t, bt, idx)
        bp = np.where(t < bt[0], (t - bt[0]) / p0, bp)
        bp = np.where(t > bt[-1], len(bt) - 1 + (t - bt[-1]) / p1, bp)
        self.beatpos = bp                                   # continuous beat index
        first_down = int(np.argmax(self.beat_down))
        self.barpos = (bp - first_down) / 4.0 + self.beat_bar[first_down]   # continuous bar index
        self.beat_frac = bp - np.floor(bp)
        self.bpm = 60.0 / np.interp(t, bt[1:], np.diff(bt), left=p0, right=p1)
        self.beat_period = 60.0 / self.bpm

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- per-frame bands
        F = T['frames']
        self.bands = {k: np.array(F[k], dtype=np.float32) for k in ['sub', 'bass', 'lowmid', 'highmid', 'high', 'loud', 'lead', 'centroid', 'flux']}
        self.silent = np.array(F['silent'], dtype=np.float32)
        self.pitch_class = np.array(F['pitch_class'])
        self.spec32 = np.array(T['spectrum32'], dtype=np.float32)
        att, rel = 0.65, 0.09
        self.s = {k: _smooth_ar(v, att, rel) for k, v in self.bands.items()}
        self.s_slow = {k: _smooth_ar(v, 0.08, 0.02) for k, v in self.bands.items()}
        # overall activity: loudness gated by absolute silence -> motion amplitude master
        self.activity = np.clip(_smooth_ar(self.bands['loud'] * (1 - self.silent), 0.5, 0.05), 0, 1)
        dbeat = np.r_[0, np.diff(bp)]
        self.flow = np.cumsum(dbeat * (0.15 + 0.85 * self.activity))        # energy-weighted beat time
        self.spec_s = self._smooth_spec()

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- onsets
        O = T['onsets']
        self.on = {k: (np.array(v['t']), np.array(v['s'])) for k, v in O.items()}
        self.kick = self.envelope(*self.on['kick'], tau=0.16)
        self.kick_fast = self.envelope(*self.on['kick'], tau=0.07)
        self.snare = self.envelope(*self.on['snare'], tau=0.12)
        self.hat = self.envelope(*self.on['hat'], tau=0.06)
        self.other = self.envelope(*self.on['other'], tau=0.18)
        self.beat = self.envelope(bt, np.ones(len(bt)), tau=0.14)
        self.down = self.envelope(bt[self.beat_down], np.ones(self.beat_down.sum()), tau=0.35)
        imp = T['impacts']
        self.impact = self.envelope(np.array([i['t'] for i in imp]), np.clip(np.array([i['db'] for i in imp]) / 30, 0.4, 1), tau=0.5)
        # time since last event and running counts (deterministic per-event randomness / shock radii)
        self.kick_since, self.kick_idx = self.since(self.on['kick'][0])
        self.snare_since, self.snare_idx = self.since(self.on['snare'][0])
        self.hat_since, self.hat_idx = self.since(self.on['hat'][0])
        self.beat_since, _ = self.since(bt)
        self.down_since, self.down_idx = self.since(bt[self.beat_down])

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- sections & phrases
        S = T['sections']
        self.sections = S
        st = np.array([s['start'] for s in S])
        self.sec_idx = np.clip(np.searchsorted(st, t + 0.5 / fps, side='right') - 1, 0, len(S) - 1)
        s0 = st[self.sec_idx]
        s1 = np.array([S[i]['end'] for i in self.sec_idx])
        self.sec_time = t - s0
        self.sec_left = s1 - t
        self.sec_prog = np.clip((t - s0) / (s1 - s0), 0, 1)
        # section progress measured in bars (for countdowns / phrase logic)
        self.sec_bar0 = np.array([S[i]['bar0'] for i in self.sec_idx])
        self.sec_bars = np.array([S[i]['bar1'] - S[i]['bar0'] for i in self.sec_idx])
        self.sec_change = self.envelope(st[1:], np.ones(len(st) - 1), tau=0.6)
        self.sec_since, _ = self.since(st[1:])
        P = T['phrases']
        pt = np.array([p['t'] for p in P])
        pl = np.array([p['level'] for p in P])
        self.phrase = self.envelope(pt, pl / 4.0, tau=0.9)
        self.phrase_since, self.phrase_idx = self.since(pt)
        self.phrase_level = np.where(self.phrase_idx >= 0, pl[np.clip(self.phrase_idx, 0, len(pl) - 1)], 0)

        # travel distance for highway mapping (per section speed profiles are applied in scenes)
        self.frame_of = lambda tt: np.clip(np.round(np.asarray(tt) * fps).astype(int), 0, n - 1)

    def _smooth_spec(self):
        out = np.empty_like(self.spec32)
        acc = self.spec32[0].copy()
        for i in range(len(self.spec32)):
            v = self.spec32[i]
            acc += (v - acc) * np.where(v > acc, 0.7, 0.12)
            out[i] = acc
        return out

    def envelope(self, times, strength, tau):
        """Jump to strength on the frame nearest the event, exponential decay afterwards."""
        n, fps = self.n, self.fps
        y = np.zeros(n, np.float32)
        if len(times) == 0:
            return y
        fr = np.round(np.asarray(times) * fps).astype(int)
        imp = np.zeros(n)
        tev = np.full(n, -1.0)
        for f, s, te in zip(fr, strength, times):
            if 0 <= f < n and s >= imp[f]:
                imp[f] = s
                tev[f] = te
        acc = 0.0
        dec = np.exp(-1.0 / (fps * tau))
        for i in range(n):
            acc *= dec
            if imp[i] > 0:
                # value at this frame measured from the true event time (never below full on its own frame)
                acc = max(acc, imp[i] * min(1.0, np.exp(-max(0.0, self.t[i] - tev[i]) / tau)))
            y[i] = acc
        return y

    def since(self, times):
        """Seconds since the last event whose nearest frame has been reached, and its index (-1 before first)."""
        fr = np.round(np.asarray(times) * self.fps).astype(int)
        k = np.searchsorted(fr, np.arange(self.n), side='right') - 1
        ts = np.where(k >= 0, self.t - np.asarray(times)[np.clip(k, 0, max(0, len(fr) - 1))], 99.0)
        return np.maximum(ts, 0.0), k

    # convenience for scenes -------------------------------------------------
    def section(self, f):
        return self.sections[self.sec_idx[f]]

    def spec_at(self, times):
        f = self.frame_of(times)
        return self.spec32[f]

    def band_at(self, name, times):
        return self.bands[name][self.frame_of(times)]

    def wave(self, f, n=1024, stereo=False, trigger=True):
        """Raw waveform window for frame f, for oscilloscope-style visuals (48 kHz float, roughly -1..1).

        Returns (n,) mono, or (n, 2) L/R with stereo=True (plot L against R for an XY / Lissajous scope).
        The window is centred on the frame time. trigger=True shifts it (by at most n/4) to the nearest rising
        zero crossing of the low-passed mono signal, like a hardware scope trigger, so periodic tones draw a
        stable trace instead of jittering. Loaded lazily from audio.wav next to timeline.json.
        """
        if self._pcm is None:
            import soundfile as sf
            x, self._sr = sf.read(self.audio_path, dtype='float32', always_2d=True)
            if x.shape[1] == 1:
                x = np.repeat(x, 2, axis=1)
            self._pcm = x[:, :2]
            k = max(1, int(self._sr / 2000))                  # ~1 kHz low-pass, used only to find the trigger
            self._trig = np.convolve(self._pcm.mean(axis=1), np.ones(k) / k, mode='same')
        x, sr = self._pcm, self._sr
        s0 = int(round(self.t[f] * sr)) - n // 2
        if trigger:
            lo, hi = max(1, s0 - n // 4), min(len(x) - 1, s0 + n // 4)
            seg = self._trig[lo - 1:hi]
            zc = np.nonzero((seg[:-1] < 0) & (seg[1:] >= 0))[0] + lo
            if len(zc):
                s0 = int(zc[np.argmin(np.abs(zc - s0))])
        w = x[np.clip(np.arange(s0, s0 + n), 0, len(x) - 1)]
        return w if stereo else w.mean(axis=1)

"""Cover art -> palette candidates.

    python cover_palette.py COVER.jpg [--k 6] [--out W/cover_palette.png]

Prints the k dominant colours (k-means in Lab-ish space on a downscaled copy) sorted by area, each with its share,
sRGB hex, a ready-to-paste linear-RGB numpy literal, and a luminance / chroma hint (ground, primary, highlight or
accent candidate). Writes a swatch strip next to the cover so one Read shows cover + palette.
Use it as raw material: the darkest large cluster usually becomes the ground, saturated mid-share clusters the
primaries, a small bright or saturated cluster the escalation accent. Lift line colours to ~1.0 so they bloom.
"""
import argparse
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument('cover')
ap.add_argument('--k', type=int, default=6)
ap.add_argument('--out', default=None)
a = ap.parse_args()

img = Image.open(a.cover).convert('RGB')
small = np.asarray(img.resize((160, int(160 * img.height / img.width))), dtype=np.float32) / 255.0
px = small.reshape(-1, 3)
lin = np.where(px <= 0.04045, px / 12.92, ((px + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4)
# cheap perceptual space: cube-root luminance-ish coordinates so dark tones do not all collapse into one cluster
feat = np.cbrt(lin)

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
C = feat[rng.choice(len(feat), a.k, replace=False)]
for _ in range(40):
    lab = np.argmin(((feat[:, None] - C[None]) ** 2).sum(-1), axis=1)
    for j in range(a.k):
        m = lab == j
        C[j] = feat[m].mean(0) if m.any() else feat[rng.integers(len(feat))]
share = np.bincount(lab, minlength=a.k) / len(lab)
order = np.argsort(-share)

rows = []
for j in order:
    cl = lin[lab == j].mean(0) if share[j] > 0 else C[j] ** 3
    srgb = np.where(cl <= 0.0031308, cl * 12.92, 1.055 * cl ** (1 / 2.4) - 0.055)
    lum = float(cl @ [0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722])
    chroma = float(srgb.max() - srgb.min())
    role = 'ground' if lum < 0.02 else 'accent' if chroma > 0.55 and share[j] < 0.12 else \
        'highlight' if lum > 0.45 else 'primary' if chroma > 0.25 else 'neutral'
    hexc = '#' + ''.join(f'{int(round(v * 255)):02x}' for v in np.clip(srgb, 0, 1))
    norm = cl / max(cl.max(), 1e-6)
    rows.append((share[j], hexc, cl, norm, lum, chroma, role, srgb))
    print(f'{share[j] * 100:5.1f}%  {hexc}  linear=np.array([{cl[0]:.3f}, {cl[1]:.3f}, {cl[2]:.3f}])  '
          f'line(~1.0)=np.array([{norm[0]:.2f}, {norm[1]:.2f}, {norm[2]:.2f}])  lum {lum:.3f} chroma {chroma:.2f}  -> {role}')

out = a.out or a.cover.rsplit('.', 1)[0] + '_palette.png'
H = 360
cov = img.resize((int(H * img.width / img.height), H))
sheet = Image.new('RGB', (cov.width + 120 * len(rows), H), (0, 0, 0))
sheet.paste(cov, (0, 0))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
for i, r in enumerate(rows):
    x = cov.width + 120 * i
    d.rectangle([x, 0, x + 119, H - 60], fill=tuple(int(v * 255) for v in np.clip(r[7], 0, 1)))
    d.text((x + 6, H - 54), f'{r[1]}\n{r[0] * 100:.0f}%  {r[6]}', fill=(230, 230, 230))
sheet.save(out)
print('wrote', out)

**Hard rules for every video:**
1. **The title sets the theme.** The world, the topic, the palette and the motif start from what the song title means. The title comes from the user, else the file tags, else the file name (`analyze.py` cleans it: `03_night_blur_master.wav` -> "Night Blur", `Artist - Title.wav` -> both).
