---
name: music-visualizer
description: Turn a song file (mp3/wav/flac/m4a) into a cinematic, beat-synced music visualizer video - Full HD 60 fps H.264/AAC MP4 ready for YouTube. Ships a working pipeline so you don't start from scratch - audio analysis to timeline.json (BPM, beat grid, downbeats, phrases, kick/snare/hat onsets, per-frame band energies, labelled sections), a reusable GPU engine (glowing 3D vector lines with depth of field, fluid simulation, bloom, shockwaves, iris transitions), a render driver that muxes audio, and automatic sync + photosensitivity verification with delivery notes. Use it whenever someone wants a music video, official visualizer, audio-reactive or beat-synced animation, spectrum video, or "visuals for my track", even if they never say "visualizer".
---

# Music visualizer

A proven pipeline: **analyze -> inspect -> art-direct one scene module -> stills -> debug preview -> verify -> full render -> notes.**
The generic parts (analysis, signal layer, GPU engine, render/mux, verification, notes) are finished scripts in `scripts/`.
Your per-song work is the **art direction**: a palette, a motif, and one `scene.py` module. Spend tokens there, not on re-deriving plumbing.

## Bundled files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `scripts/setup.sh` | creates `WORK/venv` with librosa, moderngl, soundfile (numpy/scipy/PIL/matplotlib from the system) |
| `scripts/analyze.py` | song -> `audio.wav` (48 kHz, the ONLY audio used for analysis and mux) + `timeline.json` |
| `scripts/inspect_analysis.py` | prints tempo, sections, per-bar table; writes `analysis.png` (spectrogram + sections + bands + zoom) |
| `scripts/timeline.py` | signal layer: per-frame envelopes (instant attack), A/R-smoothed bands, `beatpos`, `flow`, section progress, phrase info, arcade counters |
| `scripts/gfx.py` | GPU engine: `Camera`, `Lines`, `circle_pts`, `rot`, `Fluid`, `Engine` (bg/stars/nebula, lines with DOF, HUD layer, post chain) |
| `scripts/vfont.py` | stroke font (A-Z, 0-9, symbols): text becomes glowing line segments; `draw_on` for beam write-on |
| `scripts/render.py` | stills / clips / full render, `--debug` sync overlay, fluid warm-up, ffmpeg pipe with audio mux |
| `scripts/contact_sheet.py` | tiles stills into one image, so one Read reviews 12-16 frames |
| `scripts/verify_sync.py` | measures the MP4: stream specs, lag of visual hits per onset type, mute-test proxy, audio-vs-source alignment, flashes/s |
| `scripts/make_notes.py` | delivery notes: BPM, section table, spot-check timestamps, verification results, plus your `mapping.md` |
| `examples/scene_arcade.py` | complete worked scene ("Arcade Rush"): tunnel highway, spectrogram terrain, gyroscope core, radar beat clock, countdown builds, HUD, lockup |
| `references/analysis.md` | how the analysis works, the pitfalls it already handles, how to fix a wrong tempo/downbeat/section |
| `references/engine.md` | API reference for timeline / gfx / vfont / render, post parameters, performance numbers, rendering gotchas |
| `references/design-playbook.md` | identity process, audio->visual mapping table, section treatments, escalation, transitions, photosensitivity |

## Workflow

`SK` = this skill's directory, `W` = a work directory (for example the scratchpad). All commands run from anywhere.

### 1. Setup and analysis (about 1 minute)
```bash
bash $SK/scripts/setup.sh W                          # once per machine/work dir
W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/analyze.py "song.mp3" --workdir W
W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/inspect_analysis.py --workdir W --zoom 60,64   # then Read W/analysis.png
```
Check the printout and the PNG, not raw JSON. Section boundaries should sit on audible changes (the band curves step there), the downbeat lines should carry the big transitions, and the zoom row should show kicks on the red beat lines.
If something is off (tempo octave, downbeat phase, a missed or extra section), read `references/analysis.md`; the fixes are parameter-level.
Title and artist come from the file tags (`--title/--artist` override). The cover art is often embedded: `ffmpeg -i song.mp3 -an -c:v copy W/cover.jpg`. Look at it before designing.

### 2. Art direction (think here; this is where the quality comes from)
Read `references/design-playbook.md`. Decide and write down in `W/mapping.md`:
- the identity: 4-6 palette colors (linear RGB), ONE motif that recurs in every section, a type treatment
- the audio -> visual table (kick / snare / hat / beat / downbeat / phrase / sub / mids / highs / loudness / section)
- one treatment per section type, and how each repeat escalates (drop 1 < drop 2 < finale)

### 3. Scene module
Copy `examples/scene_arcade.py` to `W/scene.py` and re-art-direct it. Keep its structural patterns (they are what makes sync exact): the highway depth mapping, envelopes from `timeline.py`, cyclic motion from `beatpos` at 1/4-4 beats per cycle, phrase-indexed camera changes, the iris transition on section starts, HUD on its own layer.
Contract: `class Scene(tl, eng)` with `render(f)`; optional `fluid(f)` for warm-up. See `references/engine.md`.

### 4. Look development with stills (cheap)
```bash
W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/render.py --workdir W --scene W/scene.py --stills 12,40.3,55,76,100,131,170,203.5
W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/contact_sheet.py W/stills W/sheet.png 4       # Read one image
```
Pick one still per section, plus drop starts about 2 frames in. Iterate here until every section reads. The usual first-pass problems and their fixes are in `references/engine.md` under "Gotchas".

### 5. Debug preview of the most complex section
```bash
W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/render.py --workdir W --scene W/scene.py --start 138 --end 158 --debug --preset veryfast --out W/debug.mp4
```
The overlay shows the scrolling beat/downbeat grid, typed onsets, section labels, bar.beat, band meters and onset lamps.
Pull a filmstrip around a drop (`ffmpeg -i W/debug.mp4 -vf "select='between(n,N-3,N+4)',scale=480:270" -vsync 0 W/strip/f_%02d.png`, then contact-sheet it). The drop must change on the frame nearest its timestamp, together with the kick lamp.

### 6. Verify on a clean clip, then render everything
```bash
W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/render.py --workdir W --scene W/scene.py --start 138 --end 158 --preset veryfast --out W/clip.mp4
W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/verify_sync.py --workdir W --video W/clip.mp4 --offset 138
W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/render.py --workdir W --scene W/scene.py --out W/final.mp4    # run in background
W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/verify_sync.py --workdir W --video W/final.mp4
W/venv/bin/python $SK/scripts/make_notes.py --workdir W --video W/final.mp4 --mapping W/mapping.md --out W/NOTES.md
```

## Environment notes
- **GPU needs the sandbox off.** On macOS, `moderngl.create_standalone_context()` fails inside the Claude Code sandbox with "cannot choose pixel format". Run render, stills and smoke tests with the sandbox disabled. Analysis and verification run fine sandboxed.
- **Speed.** On an M1 Max a 1080p60 render runs at about 20-28 fps (libx264 `slow`, CRF 18), so a 3.5-minute song takes about 10 minutes. Always run the full render in the background.
- The output is H.264 High, yuv420p, BT.709 tv-range tags, CRF 18, AAC 320k 48 kHz, `+faststart`. Grain plus TPDF dither in the final shader prevents banding.

## Rules that keep it honest (and why)
- **Every moving parameter reads the timeline.** Cyclic motion uses `tl.beatpos` (phase-locked); non-cyclic drift uses `tl.flow` or highway travel scaled by `tl.activity`, so silence means stillness. Never use a raw clock. That is what makes a muted viewer able to tap along.
- **Hits happen on the transient frame.** Envelopes jump on the frame nearest the event and only decay afterwards. Beats are snapped to kick transients, so kick, beat and section visuals share a frame. Do not smooth event envelopes; smooth only continuous bands (fast attack, slow release).
- **The highway trick.** Place anything that "arrives" at depth `D(te) - D(t) + ZS`, where `D` is integrated travel. It crosses the strike plane exactly when it sounds, at any speed, including during accelerating builds.
- **Transitions land on the boundary frame.** Start iris wipes and surges at `sec_time == 0`. Anticipation (a build's suction, countdowns) may precede the boundary, but the change itself may not.
- **Photosensitivity.** Keep full-screen additive flashes tiny (<= 0.02 linear); use exposure surges instead, which keep contrast. Put strobing detail in small elements, and check `max_flashes_per_second`.
- **Title-safe.** HUD text stays within 90% of the frame (|x| <= 864, |y| <= 486 px from the centre at 1080p).

## Token-saving habits
- Review frames via contact sheets and filmstrips, never one PNG per Read.
- Print compact tables (`inspect_analysis.py`) instead of dumping JSON.
- Edit scene parameters surgically (small python/sed replacements) and re-render only the affected stills.
- Do not re-derive the analysis heuristics or the engine. If they fail on a song, fix the specific parameter the references point to.

## 1. Identity in 10 minutes
1. **Sources.** The embedded cover art, the title and the genre and mood read from the analysis (tempo, sub weight, brightness from centroid, lead presence, structure). Summarise the mood in 3 words.
2. **Palette.** 1 near-black ground, 2 primaries, 1 highlight for highs, 1 escalation accent held back for the biggest moments. Use linear RGB; line colours around 1.0 bloom nicely.
3. **One motif** that can become everything: HUD element, tunnel gate, sun/horizon object, map, final lockup. Examples: reticle (sci-fi or arcade), ring, chevron, glyph, waveform loop, flower of lines, pixel block, orbit. The motif is what makes separate sections feel like one world.

input.new_string:
## 1. Identity in 10 minutes
1. **Title first.** The song title is the brief. Write down:
   - its literal reading: the objects, places and phenomena it names;
   - its figurative reading: the feeling, story or metaphor;
   - a translation if it is not English. For example, "Ngizula" is Zulu for "I wander".
   Pick the reading that also fits the sound, and turn it into a world: where the camera is, what it moves through, what the light is.
   Examples: "Event Horizon" -> a fall into a black hole, lensed light. "Night Blur" -> a night motorway at a slow shutter, light trails. "Bad Boys" -> a night pursuit, sirens, a badge.
   The palette and the motif come from this world (the colour of that place and its light, the one object that stands for it). A generic abstract look is only acceptable when the title is abstract too.
2. **Cover (if any).** The cover refines, it does not replace, the title's world:
   - Run `cover_palette.py` and take the ground and primaries from its largest clusters and the accent from a small saturated one, adjusting hue so they suit the world.
   - Borrow one visual idea from its imagery: a shape, a texture, a composition or a light direction, ideally as the motif or its rendering.
   - If the cover and the title's world disagree, keep the title's world and use the cover's colours.
3. **Audio.** The genre and mood from the analysis (tempo, sub weight, brightness from the centroid, lead presence, structure) set energy and pacing: how fast the world moves, how heavy it feels, how often it cuts. Summarise the mood in 3 words.
4. **Palette.** 1 near-black ground, 2 primaries, 1 highlight for highs, 1 escalation accent held back for the biggest moments. Use linear RGB; line colours around 1.0 bloom nicely.
5. **One motif** from the title's world that can become everything: tunnel gate, sun or horizon object, map, build tension device, final lockup. Examples: reticle (sci-fi or arcade), ring, chevron, glyph, waveform loop, flower of lines, pixel block, orbit, aperture, badge, bead diamond. The motif is what makes separate sections feel like one world.
6. **Type: the title and the artist only.** They appear twice: a reveal in the intro and the lockup at the end. They may also return briefly at a big moment (for example the finale), still only as title and artist.
   - Never write lyrics, slogans, slam words, section names, numbers, BPM, captions or labels, and never use in-world signage with words.
   - The stroke font suits vector, retro-tech and minimal styles (it can glow, draw on and shatter). For other styles, render the two strings to a texture with PIL and composite them, keeping one family.
   - With no artist known, use the title alone.

# Design playbook

## 1. Identity in 10 minutes
1. **Sources.** The embedded cover art, the title and the genre and mood read from the analysis (tempo, sub weight, brightness from centroid, lead presence, structure). Summarise the mood in 3 words.
2. **Palette.** 1 near-black ground, 2 primaries, 1 highlight for highs, 1 escalation accent held back for the biggest moments. Use linear RGB; line colours around 1.0 bloom nicely.
3. **One motif** that can become everything: HUD element, tunnel gate, sun/horizon object, map, final lockup. Examples: reticle (sci-fi or arcade), ring, chevron, glyph, waveform loop, flower of lines, pixel block, orbit. The motif is what makes separate sections feel like one world.
4. **Type.** The stroke font suits vector, retro-tech and minimal styles (it can glow, draw on and shatter). For other styles, render text to a texture with PIL and composite (add a textured-quad layer), but keep one family.
5. **Camera grammar.** Decide per section: static, push, orbit, fly-over, top-down. Cuts happen only on phrase boundaries; everything else is eased moves driven by phrase progress plus beat-locked sway.

## 2. Audio -> visual mapping (template; fill in per song in mapping.md)
| Audio feature | Visual response (keep it consistent all song) |
|---|---|
| kick | arriving gate hits the strike plane; scale punch (`kick`); camera shake (`kick_fast` x sub); shockwave refraction ring; fluid radial burst |
| snare / clap | panel flash + shape reveal (polygon faces), small exposure surge (never a big full-screen flash) |
| hi-hat | sparks and particle bursts, star twinkle, ticks on the motif, letter reveals |
| beat | every beat ring flares at the strike plane; HUD beat lamps (downbeat larger) |
| downbeat | brighter rings, core ring flash, words arriving |
| phrase (4/8/16 bars) | camera angle cut or roll change, palette hue notch, add a layer |
| section | new visual state via an iris wipe from the motif, landing on the boundary frame, exposure surge + shock |
| sub / bass | mass: tunnel radius and pressure, terrain displacement, FOV breathing, camera shake depth |
| mids / lead | fluid emitters (bar-locked orbits), hue drift by pitch class / centroid, typography weight and brightness |
| highs | sparkle, particle density, star twinkle, edge ticks; a filtered-away top end means defocus |
| loudness | exposure, density, travel speed (`activity`); silence means stillness |

## 3. Section treatments (from the reference scene; reuse and re-skin)
- **Highway tunnel (drops).** Rings on the 16th grid (level-weighted: downbeat > beat > 8th > 16th), each ring's radius shaped by the spectrum at its own time, so the approaching music is visible. Kick gates are motif rings; hat sparks on the walls; snare panels; bass chevrons; speed streaks. Camera roll changes per phrase; beat-locked sway.
- **Spectrogram terrain (choruses).** Rows on the grid and columns as frequency bands (bass far, highs near the road), heights from `spec_s` at each row's time, kick ripple along the ground. A motif "sun" at the horizon carries a spectrum ring. Words arrive on downbeats and shatter on impact. Escalate with a mirrored ceiling (canyon) and the accent colour.
- **Gyroscope core (verses).** Motif rings rotating at 4 / 2 / -4 beats per revolution, an icosahedron that flashes on snares, an equatorial radial spectrum, orbiting particles lit in sequence by hats, an orbit camera that cuts per phrase, strong depth of field.
- **Radar beat clock (bridge).** Top-down view: the sweep turns once per bar, and onsets are plotted at their bar position (radius = type), so the sweep hits each blip as it sounds and phosphor afterglow draws the rhythm's mandala. Monochrome amber palette, the camera rises to reveal scale: a perspective, palette and scale shift in one.
- **Builds.** Travel speed ramps with progress squared (the highway keeps sync), FOV tightens, ticks double each bar, countdown numerals per bar (bars remaining), zoom blur and chromatic aberration rise, the grade warms, a final-beat suction (exposure dip + negative barrel), then the drop.
- **Breakdown (filtered top end).** Aperture and focus follow `1 - high`: the picture loses focus as the filter closes and snaps back as it opens. Desaturate with it.
- **Outro.** Motion amplitude follows `activity` to zero; a lockup (motif + title + artist) draws on over about 1.5 beats and then holds completely still until the end.
- **Intro.** Near-silence is a single pip. The motif draws on over the first bars, hats add ticks, sub swells send pressure rings, and the title types on one letter per hat after the first phrase of 8 s or more, with the artist on the next phrase.

## 4. Escalation of repeats
Same treatment with more of it: more layers from the first frame, a faster travel speed, the escalation accent colour, a mirrored or extra geometry layer, a stronger fluid, a bigger slam word or multiplier ("RUSH", "RUSH x2", "RUSH x3"). Keep the language identical so viewers recognise the repeat.

## 5. Transitions
An iris wipe from the motif's centre (`mix_mode=1, iris_r = ease_out(sec_time / len) * 1.15`) starts exactly on the boundary; its length is 1 beat, or 0.35 beat for drops. Render the previous look into slot 0 and the new one into slot 1 only during the wipe. Add an exposure surge plus a big shock ring on the same frame. Continuity comes from the motif and the shared highway (the verse keeps a dim tunnel behind its core).

## 6. Photosensitivity and polish
- At most 3 flashes per second in any 25%-area region (verified). Additive full-screen flashes should stay at or below 0.02 linear; use exposure surges.
- Avoid saturated red full-screen changes. Keep ember/magenta for small elements.
- Grain about 0.014 plus TPDF dither (already in the final shader) against banding. Use vignette 0.35-0.45 and subtle scanlines (0.03-0.06) for a CRT or vector feel.
- Title-safe: HUD corners at +-820 x +-440 px.
- The final frame must be a clean, readable lockup. Check the last still (t = duration - 0.1).

# Design playbook

   - its literal reading: the objects, places and phenomena it names;
   - its figurative reading: the feeling, story or metaphor;

## 3. Base visualizations: spectrogram and oscilloscope
A literal picture of the sound is a strong starting point. Build the title's world on top of it, so the scope or spectrum becomes part of the place rather than a widget.
- **Spectrogram** (`tl.spec_s[f]` = 32 smoothed bands now; `tl.spec_at(times)` = the bands at other times):
  - Terrain or waterfall: rows are time, columns are frequency. Sample each row at the moment it reaches the camera (highway depth), so the music ahead is visible.
  - Other forms: a radial spectrum ring around the motif, a skyline whose buildings are bands, tunnel rings shaped by the spectrum at their own time, bead or fringe lengths, mountain ridges, city lights.
  - Map bass to the far or back side, highs near the camera.
- **Oscilloscope** (`tl.wave(f, n, stereo=False, trigger=True)` = raw 48 kHz samples around frame f):
  - Triggered trace: `trigger=True` aligns the window to a rising zero crossing, so tones stand still.
  - `n` sets the window: 512-1024 gives a crisp waveform, 2048-4096 the envelope texture.
  - Normalise by `max(0.05, abs(w).max())` so quiet passages stay small but visible.
  - Taper the ends with a sine window when the trace is pinned inside a ring.
  - Forms: a horizon line, a heartbeat across the motif, a trace wrapped around a circle (radius = R + w * amp), or a stack of past traces receding in depth (a waveform landscape).
  - **XY / Lissajous** (`stereo=True`, plot L against R, rotated 45 degrees): mono content collapses to a line and wide stereo blooms into figures. It suits bridges, intros and breakdowns.
  - Draw it with `Lines.polyline` in world space (3D, gets DOF) or on the HUD layer (flat, crisp). Add afterglow by drawing the last 3-6 frames' traces dimmer.
- Keep the base visualization in at least the intro and one other section, so it reads as a thread through the video; escalate it (more layers, mirrored, extruded to 3D) instead of replacing it.

## 4. Section treatments (from the reference scene; reuse and re-skin)

   - a translation if it is not English. For example, "Ngizula" is Zulu for "I wander".

2. **Cover (if any).** The cover refines, it does not replace, the title's world:
   - Run `cover_palette.py` and take the ground and primaries from its largest clusters and the accent from a small saturated one, adjusting hue so they suit the world.
   - Borrow one visual idea from its imagery: a shape, a texture, a composition or a light direction, ideally as the motif or its rendering.
   - If the cover and the title's world disagree, keep the title's world and use the cover's colours.
3. **Audio.** The genre and mood from the analysis (tempo, sub weight, brightness from the centroid, lead presence, structure) set energy and pacing: how fast the world moves, how heavy it feels, how often it cuts. Summarise the mood in 3 words.
4. **Palette.** 1 near-black ground, 2 primaries, 1 highlight for highs, 1 escalation accent held back for the biggest moments. Use linear RGB; line colours around 1.0 bloom nicely.
5. **One motif** from the title's world that can become everything: tunnel gate, sun or horizon object, map, build tension device, final lockup. Examples: reticle (sci-fi or arcade), ring, chevron, glyph, waveform loop, flower of lines, pixel block, orbit, aperture, badge, bead diamond. The motif is what makes separate sections feel like one world.
6. **Type: the title and the artist only.** They appear twice: a reveal in the intro and the lockup at the end. They may also return briefly at a big moment (for example the finale), still only as title and artist.
   - Never write lyrics, slogans, slam words, section names, numbers, BPM, captions or labels, and never use in-world signage with words.
   - The stroke font suits vector, retro-tech and minimal styles (it can glow, draw on and shatter). For other styles, render the two strings to a texture with PIL and composite them, keeping one family.
   - With no artist known, use the title alone.
7. **Camera grammar.** Decide per section: static, push, orbit, fly-over, top-down. Cuts happen only on phrase boundaries; everything else is eased moves driven by phrase progress plus beat-locked sway.

|---|---|

| hi-hat | sparks and particle bursts, star twinkle, ticks on the motif, title letter reveals in the intro |
| beat | every beat ring flares at the strike plane; a pulse on a LARGE scene element (never a lamp, counter or meter) |
| downbeat | brighter rings, core ring flash, a new layer or object arriving |
| phrase (4/8/16 bars) | camera angle cut or roll change, palette hue notch, add a layer |
| section | new visual state via an iris wipe from the motif, landing on the boundary frame, exposure surge + shock |
| sub / bass | mass: tunnel radius and pressure, terrain displacement, FOV breathing, camera shake depth |
| mids / lead | fluid emitters (bar-locked orbits), hue drift by pitch class / centroid, title stroke weight and brightness while it is up |
| highs | sparkle, particle density, star twinkle, edge ticks; a filtered-away top end means defocus |
| loudness | exposure, density, travel speed (`activity`); silence means stillness |

- **Highway tunnel (drops).** Rings on the 16th grid (level-weighted: downbeat > beat > 8th > 16th), each ring's radius shaped by the spectrum at its own time, so the approaching music is visible. Kick gates are motif rings; hat sparks on the walls; snare panels; bass chevrons; speed streaks. Camera roll changes per phrase; beat-locked sway.

# Engine and signal-layer reference

## timeline.Timeline(path) — per-frame arrays (length n = frames)
- clocks: `t`, `beatpos` (continuous beat index), `barpos`, `beat_frac`, `bpm`, `beat_period`, `flow` (beat time x activity)
- bands: `bands[k]` raw, `s[k]` fast-attack/slow-release, `s_slow[k]` (k in sub, bass, lowmid, highmid, high, loud, lead, centroid, flux); `spec32`, `spec_s` (smoothed); `pitch_class`; `activity` (loudness gated by silence = master motion amplitude)
- envelopes (instant attack on nearest frame, exp decay): `kick` (tau 0.16), `kick_fast` (0.07), `snare`, `hat`, `other`, `beat`, `down`, `impact`, `sec_change`, `phrase` (level-weighted)
- since/index: `kick_since`, `kick_idx`, `snare_*`, `hat_*`, `beat_since`, `down_*`, `phrase_since`, `phrase_idx`, `phrase_level`, `sec_since`
- sections: `sec_idx`, `sec_time`, `sec_left`, `sec_prog`, `sections` (raw dicts), `section(f)`
- onsets: `on[k] = (times, strengths)`; `beat_t`, `beat_down`, `beat_bar`, `beat_inbar`
- arcade counters: `score` (kick 100 / snare 50 / hat 10, cumulative), `combo` (consecutive beats that had a kick)
- helpers: `envelope(times, strengths, tau)`, `since(times)`, `frame_of(times)`, `spec_at(times)`

## gfx
- `Camera(eye, target, up, fov, roll, focus, aperture, near, far)`. `aperture` > 0 gives line depth of field (CoC px = aperture * f_px * |1/z - 1/focus|, capped by `maxcoc`).
- `Lines()`: `.add(a[N,3], b[N,3], color[N,3] or [3], wpx, wworld)`, `.polyline(pts, color, wpx, closed)`. Colors are linear HDR (values > 1 bloom). Width = pixels + world units (perspective).
- `circle_pts(center, r, n, u, v, a0, a1, radii)`, `rot(axis, angle)`, `look_at`, `perspective`.
- `Fluid(ctx, sim, dye)`: `.splat(x, y, vx, vy, rgb, radius)` (uv, y up; velocity in sim texels/s), `.step(curl, vel_diss, dye_diss, iters)`, `.dye_tex`. Stateful: render sequentially, or warm up (render.py does `--warmup` seconds of `scene.fluid(f)`).
- `Engine(W, H)`:
  - `begin(slot, bg, cam)` clears scene slot 0/1 and draws the sky: `sky_top, sky_bot, horizon, horizon_w, up, star_amt, star_twinkle, star_seed, neb_amt` (fluid dye as nebula), `neb_shift, neb_mask_sky` (1 = only above the horizon), `fogcol, fogamt`
  - `draw(lines, cam, fog=, gain=, maxcoc=)` additive capsules with DOF into the current slot. `draw(lines, None, hud=True)` goes to the HUD layer (pixel coordinates, origin at the centre, y up, z = -1)
  - `clear_hud()` once per frame before HUD draws
  - `finish(post)` composites slots (iris mask), bloom (6 mips), anamorphic streak, final pass. The HUD is bloomed but never distorted
  - `read()` returns RGB24 bytes, top row first
- post keys (defaults in `DEFAULT_POST`): `bloom_amt, bloom_threshold, bloom_knee, streak_amt, streak_tint, exposure, flash, flash_col, ca, barrel, zoomblur, center, shocks=[(x,y,radius,strength) x <= 4], kaleido, kaleido_n, kaleido_rot, defocus, saturation, lift, gain, contrast, vignette, scan, grain, fade, tint, tint_amt, mix_mode, iris_c, iris_r, edge_col, xfade, hud_gain`

## vfont
`text_segments(s, size, tracking, align)` returns `([(i, ch, segs(N,2,2), cx)], width)`; `draw_on(segs, p)`; glyphs A-Z, 0-9, `- . : / ! ? + x > < [ ] # '` and space (lowercase maps to uppercase; `x` is the multiplication sign).

## render.py CLI
`--workdir --scene [--out] [--start --end] [--stills t1,t2] [--debug] [--warmup 4] [--crf 18] [--preset slow] [--width --height]`

## Performance (M1 Max, 1080p60)
Engine init 0.2 s. A simple scene takes 11 ms per frame. The full Arcade Rush scene (20-40k segments, fluid 320x180 / 960x540 with 22 Jacobi iterations, 2 scene slots during transitions) runs at 20-28 fps including libx264 `slow`. Numpy geometry is the main CPU cost; keep it vectorised (one `.add` per layer, never per segment in Python loops when N > ~50).

## Gotchas already hit (and fixes)
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| GL context: "cannot choose pixel format" | sandbox blocks the GPU | run render commands with the sandbox disabled |
| White blob at the vanishing point / horizon band | additive lines pile up where far geometry converges | fog 0.006+, FAR <= 380, per-row `exp(-d/110..140)` fade, dimmer far gates |
| Whole frame turns beige on drops | additive flash lifts blacks massively after ACES + sRGB | exposure surge `exposure *= 1 + 0.9*surge`, additive flash <= 0.012 |
| HUD text mangled by zoom blur / kaleidoscope | HUD in the distorted scene | draw HUD with `hud=True` (own layer) |
| Ghost copies of HUD text | kaleidoscope folds the bloom (which includes the HUD) | avoid kaleido while big HUD text is up, or skip kaleido |
| Starfield like snow | too many stars | threshold 0.955, sharp falloff (already set) |
| Kick flash one frame before the section cut | grid beat vs kick straddle a frame | beats snapped to kicks in analyze.py (already done) |
| Muddy smoke everywhere | fluid dye too strong | kick dye ~0.045*s, lead ~0.012, `dye_diss` 0.9-1.7, `neb_amt` 0.45-0.9 |
| Mountains off-screen, flat ground | terrain too wide for the FOV | columns within +-70 units, camera at y 4-5 looking slightly down |
| One-frame section "slivers" | segmentation leftovers | handled in analyze (min lengths); re-inspect after tuning |
| 3 flashes/s at the build->drop hand-off | countdown beat pulses + suction dip + drop surge stack up within 1 s | beat pulse <= 0.7, suction <= 0.2, surge <= 0.6 (verify reports the worst window) |
| 3 flashes/s during snare rolls | snare-driven bloom on a big central object | keep snare gain on large bright shapes ~1x, push the accent into small elements |
| Beats "without a visible hit" in sparse sections | only the tiny HUD lamps react | add a small per-beat pulse to a large element (ring width/brightness) in intro/bridge |
| A/V end window reports tens of ms | waveform correlation on a sustained decaying chord is ambiguous | verify anchors windows on kicks (fixed); spot-check with a transient window if in doubt |

- since/index: `kick_since`, `kick_idx`, `snare_*`, `hat_*`, `beat_since`, `down_*`, `phrase_since`, `phrase_idx`, `phrase_level`, `sec_since`
- sections: `sec_idx`, `sec_time`, `sec_left`, `sec_prog`, `sections` (raw dicts), `section(f)`
- onsets: `on[k] = (times, strengths)`; `beat_t`, `beat_down`, `beat_bar`, `beat_inbar`
- helpers: `envelope(times, strengths, tau)`, `since(times)`, `frame_of(times)`, `spec_at(times)`, `band_at(name, times)`
- `wave(f, n=1024, stereo=False, trigger=True)`: raw 48 kHz samples around frame f from `audio.wav` (lazy-loaded), `(n,)` mono or `(n, 2)` L/R. `trigger` snaps the window (at most n/4) to the nearest rising zero crossing of a ~1 kHz low-passed copy, giving a stable scope trace. Use it for oscilloscopes, circular scopes and XY / Lissajous (L against R).
- `title`, `artist` (artist may be `''`: then draw the title alone). These are the only strings a scene may render.

## gfx
- `Camera(eye, target, up, fov, roll, focus, aperture, near, far)`. `aperture` > 0 gives line depth of field (CoC px = aperture * f_px * |1/z - 1/focus|, capped by `maxcoc`).
- `Lines()`: `.add(a[N,3], b[N,3], color[N,3] or [3], wpx, wworld)`, `.polyline(pts, color, wpx, closed)`. Colors are linear HDR (values > 1 bloom). Width = pixels + world units (perspective).
- `circle_pts(center, r, n, u, v, a0, a1, radii)`, `rot(axis, angle)`, `look_at`, `perspective`.
- `Fluid(ctx, sim, dye)`: `.splat(x, y, vx, vy, rgb, radius)` (uv, y up; velocity in sim texels/s), `.step(curl, vel_diss, dye_diss, iters)`, `.dye_tex`. Stateful: render sequentially, or warm up (render.py does `--warmup` seconds of `scene.fluid(f)`).
- `Engine(W, H)`:
  - `begin(slot, bg, cam)` clears scene slot 0/1 and draws the sky: `sky_top, sky_bot, horizon, horizon_w, up, star_amt, star_twinkle, star_seed, neb_amt` (fluid dye as nebula), `neb_shift, neb_mask_sky` (1 = only above the horizon), `fogcol, fogamt`
  - `draw(lines, cam, fog=, gain=, maxcoc=)` additive capsules with DOF into the current slot. `draw(lines, None, hud=True)` goes to the HUD layer (pixel coordinates, origin at the centre, y up, z = -1)
  - `clear_hud()` once per frame before HUD draws
  - `finish(post)` composites slots (iris mask), bloom (6 mips), anamorphic streak, final pass. The HUD is bloomed but never distorted
  - `read()` returns RGB24 bytes, top row first
- post keys (defaults in `DEFAULT_POST`): `bloom_amt, bloom_threshold, bloom_knee, streak_amt, streak_tint, exposure, flash, flash_col, ca, barrel, zoomblur, center, shocks=[(x,y,radius,strength) x <= 4], kaleido, kaleido_n, kaleido_rot, defocus, saturation, lift, gain, contrast, vignette, scan, grain, fade, tint, tint_amt, mix_mode, iris_c, iris_r, edge_col, xfade, hud_gain`

## vfont
`text_segments(s, size, tracking, align)` returns `([(i, ch, segs(N,2,2), cx)], width)`; `draw_on(segs, p)`; glyphs A-Z, 0-9, `- . : / ! ? + x > < [ ] # '` and space (lowercase maps to uppercase; `x` is the multiplication sign).

## render.py CLI
`--workdir --scene [--out] [--start --end] [--stills t1,t2] [--debug] [--warmup 4] [--crf 18] [--preset slow] [--width --height]`

## Performance (M1 Max, 1080p60)
Engine init 0.2 s. A simple scene takes 11 ms per frame. The full Arcade Rush scene (20-40k segments, fluid 320x180 / 960x540 with 22 Jacobi iterations, 2 scene slots during transitions) runs at 20-28 fps including libx264 `slow`. Numpy geometry is the main CPU cost; keep it vectorised (one `.add` per layer, never per segment in Python loops when N > ~50).

## Gotchas already hit (and fixes)
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| GL context: "cannot choose pixel format" | sandbox blocks the GPU | run render commands with the sandbox disabled |
| White blob at the vanishing point / horizon band | additive lines pile up where far geometry converges | fog 0.006+, FAR <= 380, per-row `exp(-d/110..140)` fade, dimmer far gates |
| Whole frame turns beige on drops | additive flash lifts blacks massively after ACES + sRGB | exposure surge `exposure *= 1 + 0.9*surge`, additive flash <= 0.012 |
| Title text mangled by zoom blur / kaleidoscope | title in the distorted scene | draw the title/artist with `hud=True` (own layer) |
| Ghost copies of the title | kaleidoscope folds the bloom (which includes the HUD layer) | avoid kaleido while the title is up, or skip kaleido |
| Scope trace jitters sideways every frame | untriggered window | `tl.wave(f, trigger=True)` (default); longer `n` for noisy material |
| Scope flat in quiet passages, clipped in loud ones | fixed scaling | normalise per frame by `max(0.05, abs(w).max())` and scale amplitude by `activity` |
| Starfield like snow | too many stars | threshold 0.955, sharp falloff (already set) |
| Kick flash one frame before the section cut | grid beat vs kick straddle a frame | beats snapped to kicks in analyze.py (already done) |
| Muddy smoke everywhere | fluid dye too strong | kick dye ~0.045*s, lead ~0.012, `dye_diss` 0.9-1.7, `neb_amt` 0.45-0.9 |
| Mountains off-screen, flat ground | terrain too wide for the FOV | columns within +-70 units, camera at y 4-5 looking slightly down |
| One-frame section "slivers" | segmentation leftovers | handled in analyze (min lengths); re-inspect after tuning |
| 3 flashes/s at the build->drop hand-off | countdown beat pulses + suction dip + drop surge stack up within 1 s | beat pulse <= 0.7, suction <= 0.2, surge <= 0.6 (verify reports the worst window) |
| 3 flashes/s during snare rolls | snare-driven bloom on a big central object | keep snare gain on large bright shapes ~1x, push the accent into small elements |
| Beats "without a visible hit" in sparse sections | only the tiny HUD lamps react | add a small per-beat pulse to a large element (ring width/brightness) in intro/bridge |
| A/V end window reports tens of ms | waveform correlation on a sustained decaying chord is ambiguous | verify anchors windows on kicks (fixed); spot-check with a transient window if in doubt |

## Visual identity
Derived from the cover art (a retro sci-fi cockpit with green holographic HUD rings and amber instrument lights) and the track (a 108 BPM four-on-the-floor synth instrumental).
- **Palette:** teal-black void; phosphor green (primary lines); amber (instruments, downbeats, type); cyan for highs and sparks; ember and magenta held back for escalation (drop 2+, chorus 2); white-hot for impacts.
- **Motif:** the **targeting reticle** (rings, ticks, crosshair gaps, centre pip). It is the HUD, every kick gate in the tunnel, the horizon sun, the gyroscope core, the radar, and the final lockup.
- **Type:** a custom chamfered stroke font drawn as glowing vector lines. It draws on like an electron beam, pulses with the beat and shatters into segments.
- **Techniques:** 3D vector geometry with per-line depth of field, 2D HUD and kinetic typography, a GPU fluid simulation (nebula and smoke), particles (hat sparks, speed streaks, shattered letters), shockwave refraction, chromatic aberration, zoom blur, anamorphic streaks, bloom, iris masking between scenes, and focus pulls.

## Audio -> visual mapping
| Audio feature | Visual response |
|---|---|

Build 2 tilts down from the radar map into the tunnel |
27:| Drop (x3) | The rhythm-highway tunnel. "RUSH" slams on the first beat and shatters on the next downbeat, becoming "RUSH x2" and "RUSH x3". Drop 2 starts fully layered with ember accents and a faster speed; drop 3 adds the terrain canyon and white-hot accents |
28:| Chorus (x2) | A spectrogram mountain terrain along a road, the reticle sun with a spectrum ring, ARCADE / RUSH words arriving on downbeats, a teal fluid sky. Chorus 2 adds a mirrored ceiling (canyon), magenta accents and a faster speed |
32:| Outro | The world winds down with the final chord; the lockup (reticle + ARCADE RUSH + VOHO) draws on and holds as the clean final frame |

# Engine and signal-layer reference

## timeline.Timeline(path) — per-frame arrays (length n = frames)
- clocks: `t`, `beatpos` (continuous beat index), `barpos`, `beat_frac`, `bpm`, `beat_period`, `flow` (beat time x activity)
- bands: `bands[k]` raw, `s[k]` fast-attack/slow-release, `s_slow[k]` (k in sub, bass, lowmid, highmid, high, loud, lead, centroid, flux); `spec32`, `spec_s` (smoothed); `pitch_class`; `activity` (loudness gated by silence = master motion amplitude)
- envelopes (instant attack on nearest frame, exp decay): `kick` (tau 0.16), `kick_fast` (0.07), `snare`, `hat`, `other`, `beat`, `down`, `impact`, `sec_change`, `phrase` (level-weighted)
- since/index: `kick_since`, `kick_idx`, `snare_*`, `hat_*`, `beat_since`, `down_*`, `phrase_since`, `phrase_idx`, `phrase_level`, `sec_since`
- sections: `sec_idx`, `sec_time`, `sec_left`, `sec_prog`, `sections` (raw dicts), `section(f)`
- onsets: `on[k] = (times, strengths)`; `beat_t`, `beat_down`, `beat_bar`, `beat_inbar`
- helpers: `envelope(times, strengths, tau)`, `since(times)`, `frame_of(times)`, `spec_at(times)`, `band_at(name, times)`
- `wave(f, n=1024, stereo=False, trigger=True)`: raw 48 kHz samples around frame f from `audio.wav` (lazy-loaded), `(n,)` mono or `(n, 2)` L/R. `trigger` snaps the window (at most n/4) to the nearest rising zero crossing of a ~1 kHz low-passed copy, giving a stable scope trace. Use it for oscilloscopes, circular scopes and XY / Lissajous (L against R).
- `title`, `artist` (artist may be `''`: then draw the title alone). These are the only strings a scene may render.

## gfx
- `Camera(eye, target, up, fov, roll, focus, aperture, near, far)`. `aperture` > 0 gives line depth of field (CoC px = aperture * f_px * |1/z - 1/focus|, capped by `maxcoc`).
- `Lines()`: `.add(a[N,3], b[N,3], color[N,3] or [3], wpx, wworld)`, `.polyline(pts, color, wpx, closed)`. Colors are linear HDR (values > 1 bloom). Width = pixels + world units (perspective).
- `circle_pts(center, r, n, u, v, a0, a1, radii)`, `rot(axis, angle)`, `look_at`, `perspective`.
- `Fluid(ctx, sim, dye)`: `.splat(x, y, vx, vy, rgb, radius)` (uv, y up; velocity in sim texels/s), `.step(curl, vel_diss, dye_diss, iters)`, `.dye_tex`. Stateful: render sequentially, or warm up (render.py does `--warmup` seconds of `scene.fluid(f)`).
- `Engine(W, H)`:
  - `begin(slot, bg, cam)` clears scene slot 0/1 and draws the sky: `sky_top, sky_bot, horizon, horizon_w, up, star_amt, star_twinkle, star_seed, neb_amt` (fluid dye as nebula), `neb_shift, neb_mask_sky` (1 = only above the horizon), `fogcol, fogamt`
  - `draw(lines, cam, fog=, gain=, maxcoc=)` additive capsules with DOF into the current slot. `draw(lines, None, hud=True)` goes to the HUD layer (pixel coordinates, origin at the centre, y up, z = -1)
  - `clear_hud()` once per frame before HUD draws
  - `finish(post)` composites slots (iris mask), bloom (6 mips), anamorphic streak, final pass. The HUD is bloomed but never distorted
  - `read()` returns RGB24 bytes, top row first
- post keys (defaults in `DEFAULT_POST`): `bloom_amt, bloom_threshold, bloom_knee, streak_amt, streak_tint, exposure, flash, flash_col, ca, barrel, zoomblur, center, shocks=[(x,y,radius,strength) x <= 4], kaleido, kaleido_n, kaleido_rot, defocus, saturation, lift, gain, contrast, vignette, scan, grain, fade, tint, tint_amt, mix_mode, iris_c, iris_r, edge_col, xfade, hud_gain`

## vfont
`text_segments(s, size, tracking, align)` returns `([(i, ch, segs(N,2,2), cx)], width)`; `draw_on(segs, p)`; glyphs A-Z, 0-9, `- . : / ! ? + x > < [ ] # '` and space (lowercase maps to uppercase; `x` is the multiplication sign).

## render.py CLI
`--workdir --scene [--out] [--start --end] [--stills t1,t2] [--debug] [--warmup 4] [--crf 18] [--preset slow] [--width --height]`

## Performance (M1 Max, 1080p60)
Engine init 0.2 s. A simple scene takes 11 ms per frame. The full Arcade Rush scene (20-40k segments, fluid 320x180 / 960x540 with 22 Jacobi iterations, 2 scene slots during transitions) runs at 20-28 fps including libx264 `slow`. Numpy geometry is the main CPU cost; keep it vectorised (one `.add` per layer, never per segment in Python loops when N > ~50).

## Gotchas already hit (and fixes)
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| GL context: "cannot choose pixel format" | sandbox blocks the GPU | run render commands with the sandbox disabled |
| White blob at the vanishing point / horizon band | additive lines pile up where far geometry converges | fog 0.006+, FAR <= 380, per-row `exp(-d/110..140)` fade, dimmer far gates |
| Whole frame turns beige on drops | additive flash lifts blacks massively after ACES + sRGB | exposure surge `exposure *= 1 + 0.9*surge`, additive flash <= 0.012 |
| Title text mangled by zoom blur / kaleidoscope | title in the distorted scene | draw the title/artist with `hud=True` (own layer) |
| Ghost copies of the title | kaleidoscope folds the bloom (which includes the HUD layer) | avoid kaleido while the title is up, or skip kaleido |
| Scope trace jitters sideways every frame | untriggered window | `tl.wave(f, trigger=True)` (default); longer `n` for noisy material |
| Scope flat in quiet passages, clipped in loud ones | fixed scaling | normalise per frame by `max(0.05, abs(w).max())` and scale amplitude by `activity` |
| Starfield like snow | too many stars | threshold 0.955, sharp falloff (already set) |
| Kick flash one frame before the section cut | grid beat vs kick straddle a frame | beats snapped to kicks in analyze.py (already done) |
| Muddy smoke everywhere | fluid dye too strong | kick dye ~0.045*s, lead ~0.012, `dye_diss` 0.9-1.7, `neb_amt` 0.45-0.9 |
| Mountains off-screen, flat ground | terrain too wide for the FOV | columns within +-70 units, camera at y 4-5 looking slightly down |
| One-frame section "slivers" | segmentation leftovers | handled in analyze (min lengths); re-inspect after tuning |
| 3 flashes/s at the build->drop hand-off | countdown beat pulses + suction dip + drop surge stack up within 1 s | beat pulse <= 0.7, suction <= 0.2, surge <= 0.6 (verify reports the worst window) |
| 3 flashes/s during snare rolls | snare-driven bloom on a big central object | keep snare gain on large bright shapes ~1x, push the accent into small elements |
| Beats "without a visible hit" in sparse sections | only small elements react | add a per-beat pulse to a large element (ring width/brightness, scope amplitude, motif scale) in intro/bridge; never add beat lamps or counters |
| A/V end window reports tens of ms | waveform correlation on a sustained decaying chord is ambiguous | verify anchors windows on kicks (fixed); spot-check with a transient window if in doubt |

"""Signal layer: turns timeline.json into per-frame control signals.

Everything the renderer animates is read from here. Rules:
  * event envelopes jump to full value on the frame nearest the transient (never later), then decay
  * continuous band signals use fast attack / slow release one-pole smoothing (no added lag on rises)
  * cyclic motion uses `beatpos` (continuous beat index) so it is phase-locked to the grid
  * non-cyclic drift uses `flow`: beat time weighted by loudness, so silence means stillness
"""
import json
import os
import numpy as np


def _smooth_ar(x, att, rel):
    y = np.empty_like(x)
    acc = x[0]
    for i, v in enumerate(x):
        acc += (v - acc) * (att if v > acc else rel)
        y[i] = acc
    return y


class Timeline:
    def __init__(self, path='timeline.json'):
        T = json.load(open(path))
        self.raw = T
        self.audio_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), 'audio.wav')
        self._pcm = None
        m = T['meta']
        self.fps = m['fps']
        self.n = m['n_frames']
        self.duration = m['duration']
        self.title, self.artist = m['title'], m['artist']
        fps, n = self.fps, self.n
        self.t = np.arange(n) / fps
        t = self.t

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- beat grid clocks
        bt = np.array([b['t'] for b in T['beats']])
        self.beat_t = bt
        self.beat_down = np.array([b['downbeat'] for b in T['beats']])
        self.beat_bar = np.array([b['bar'] for b in T['beats']])
        self.beat_inbar = np.array([b['beat'] for b in T['beats']])
        idx = np.arange(len(bt), dtype=float)
        p0, p1 = bt[1] - bt[0], bt[-1] - bt[-2]
        bp = np.interp(t, bt, idx)
        bp = np.where(t < bt[0], (t - bt[0]) / p0, bp)
        bp = np.where(t > bt[-1], len(bt) - 1 + (t - bt[-1]) / p1, bp)
        self.beatpos = bp                                   # continuous beat index
        first_down = int(np.argmax(self.beat_down))
        self.barpos = (bp - first_down) / 4.0 + self.beat_bar[first_down]   # continuous bar index
        self.beat_frac = bp - np.floor(bp)
        self.bpm = 60.0 / np.interp(t, bt[1:], np.diff(bt), left=p0, right=p1)
        self.beat_period = 60.0 / self.bpm

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- per-frame bands
        F = T['frames']
        self.bands = {k: np.array(F[k], dtype=np.float32) for k in ['sub', 'bass', 'lowmid', 'highmid', 'high', 'loud', 'lead', 'centroid', 'flux']}
        self.silent = np.array(F['silent'], dtype=np.float32)
        self.pitch_class = np.array(F['pitch_class'])
        self.spec32 = np.array(T['spectrum32'], dtype=np.float32)
        att, rel = 0.65, 0.09
        self.s = {k: _smooth_ar(v, att, rel) for k, v in self.bands.items()}
        self.s_slow = {k: _smooth_ar(v, 0.08, 0.02) for k, v in self.bands.items()}
        # overall activity: loudness gated by absolute silence -> motion amplitude master
        self.activity = np.clip(_smooth_ar(self.bands['loud'] * (1 - self.silent), 0.5, 0.05), 0, 1)
        dbeat = np.r_[0, np.diff(bp)]
        self.flow = np.cumsum(dbeat * (0.15 + 0.85 * self.activity))        # energy-weighted beat time
        self.spec_s = self._smooth_spec()

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- onsets
        O = T['onsets']
        self.on = {k: (np.array(v['t']), np.array(v['s'])) for k, v in O.items()}
        self.kick = self.envelope(*self.on['kick'], tau=0.16)
        self.kick_fast = self.envelope(*self.on['kick'], tau=0.07)
        self.snare = self.envelope(*self.on['snare'], tau=0.12)
        self.hat = self.envelope(*self.on['hat'], tau=0.06)
        self.other = self.envelope(*self.on['other'], tau=0.18)
        self.beat = self.envelope(bt, np.ones(len(bt)), tau=0.14)
        self.down = self.envelope(bt[self.beat_down], np.ones(self.beat_down.sum()), tau=0.35)
        imp = T['impacts']
        self.impact = self.envelope(np.array([i['t'] for i in imp]), np.clip(np.array([i['db'] for i in imp]) / 30, 0.4, 1), tau=0.5)
        # time since last event and running counts (deterministic per-event randomness / shock radii)
        self.kick_since, self.kick_idx = self.since(self.on['kick'][0])
        self.snare_since, self.snare_idx = self.since(self.on['snare'][0])
        self.hat_since, self.hat_idx = self.since(self.on['hat'][0])
        self.beat_since, _ = self.since(bt)
        self.down_since, self.down_idx = self.since(bt[self.beat_down])

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- sections & phrases
        S = T['sections']
        self.sections = S
        st = np.array([s['start'] for s in S])
        self.sec_idx = np.clip(np.searchsorted(st, t + 0.5 / fps, side='right') - 1, 0, len(S) - 1)
        s0 = st[self.sec_idx]
        s1 = np.array([S[i]['end'] for i in self.sec_idx])
        self.sec_time = t - s0
        self.sec_left = s1 - t
        self.sec_prog = np.clip((t - s0) / (s1 - s0), 0, 1)
        # section progress measured in bars (for countdowns / phrase logic)
        self.sec_bar0 = np.array([S[i]['bar0'] for i in self.sec_idx])
        self.sec_bars = np.array([S[i]['bar1'] - S[i]['bar0'] for i in self.sec_idx])
        self.sec_change = self.envelope(st[1:], np.ones(len(st) - 1), tau=0.6)
        self.sec_since, _ = self.since(st[1:])
        P = T['phrases']
        pt = np.array([p['t'] for p in P])
        pl = np.array([p['level'] for p in P])
        self.phrase = self.envelope(pt, pl / 4.0, tau=0.9)
        self.phrase_since, self.phrase_idx = self.since(pt)
        self.phrase_level = np.where(self.phrase_idx >= 0, pl[np.clip(self.phrase_idx, 0, len(pl) - 1)], 0)

        # travel distance for highway mapping (per section speed profiles are applied in scenes)
        self.frame_of = lambda tt: np.clip(np.round(np.asarray(tt) * fps).astype(int), 0, n - 1)

    def _smooth_spec(self):
        out = np.empty_like(self.spec32)
        acc = self.spec32[0].copy()
        for i in range(len(self.spec32)):
            v = self.spec32[i]
            acc += (v - acc) * np.where(v > acc, 0.7, 0.12)
            out[i] = acc
        return out

    def envelope(self, times, strength, tau):
        """Jump to strength on the frame nearest the event, exponential decay afterwards."""
        n, fps = self.n, self.fps
        y = np.zeros(n, np.float32)
        if len(times) == 0:
            return y
        fr = np.round(np.asarray(times) * fps).astype(int)

        Returns (n,) mono, or (n, 2) L/R with stereo=True (plot L against R for an XY / Lissajous scope).
        The window is centred on the frame time. trigger=True shifts it (by at most n/4) to the nearest rising

"""Write delivery notes (markdown) from timeline.json + the verify_sync report + a song-specific mapping file.

  python make_notes.py --workdir W --video W/final.mp4 --mapping W/mapping.md --out W/NOTES.md

mapping.md is the only hand-written part: the audio-feature -> visual table and per-section art direction.
Spot-check timestamps are picked automatically: first drop downbeat, a strong mid-song kick on a downbeat,
and the last section boundary before the outro.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os

import numpy as np


def mmss(t):
    m = int(t // 60)
    return f'{m}:{t - 60 * m:06.3f}'


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument('--workdir', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--video', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--mapping', default=None)
    ap.add_argument('--out', required=True)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    T = json.load(open(os.path.join(a.workdir, 'timeline.json')))
    vpath = os.path.splitext(a.video)[0] + '_verify.json'
    V = json.load(open(vpath)) if os.path.exists(vpath) else {}
    S = T['sections']
    tp = T['tempo']
    fps = T['meta']['fps']
    L = []
    L.append(f"# {T['meta']['title']} - {T['meta']['artist']} | visualizer delivery notes\n")
    L.append(f"**File:** `{os.path.basename(a.video)}`  ")
    if V:
        v, au = V.get('video', {}), V.get('audio', {})
        L.append(f"**Video:** {v.get('codec')} {v.get('size')} @ {v.get('fps')} fps, {v.get('pix_fmt')}, {v.get('bitrate', 0) / 1e6:.1f} Mbps, "
                 f"{v.get('frames')} frames  ")
        L.append(f"**Audio:** {au.get('codec')} {au.get('rate')} Hz, {au.get('channels')} ch, {au.get('bitrate', 0) / 1000:.0f} kbps  ")
        L.append(f"**Duration:** container {V.get('container_duration'):.3f} s, song {V.get('song_duration'):.3f} s\n")
    L.append('## Tempo')
    const = 'constant - no tempo changes detected' if tp['constant'] else 'variable - motion follows the local beat grid'
    L.append(f"**{tp['bpm']:.1f} BPM**, {tp['time_signature']}, {const} (local estimate {tp['bpm_min']}-{tp['bpm_max']}). "
             f"{len(T['beats'])} beats; grid aligned to kick transients (shift {tp['grid_shift_ms']:+.1f} ms).\n")
    L.append('## Sections')
    L.append('| # | Section | Start | End | Bars |')
    L.append('|---|---|---|---|---|')
    for i, s in enumerate(S):
        L.append(f"| {i + 1} | {s['label']} {s['occurrence']} | {mmss(s['start'])} | {mmss(s['end'])} | {s['bar0'] + 1}-{s['bar1']} |")
    reps = [s for s in S if s.get('repeats') is not None]
    if reps:
        L.append('\nRepeats: ' + ', '.join(f"{s['label']} {s['occurrence']} repeats section {s['repeats'] + 1}" for s in reps) + '.\n')
    counts = {k: len(v['t']) for k, v in T['onsets'].items()}
    L.append(f"Onsets: {counts['kick']} kicks, {counts['snare']} snare/clap accents, {counts['hat']} hi-hats, {counts['other']} other hits.\n")
    if a.mapping and os.path.exists(a.mapping):
        L.append(open(a.mapping).read().strip() + '\n')
    # spot checks
    beats = np.array([b['t'] for b in T['beats']])
    down = np.array([b['downbeat'] for b in T['beats']])
    kt, ks = np.array(T['onsets']['kick']['t']), np.array(T['onsets']['kick']['s'])
    drops = [s for s in S if s['label'] in ('drop', 'chorus')]
    spots = []
    if drops:
        spots.append((drops[0]['start'], f"first {drops[0]['label']} lands - section cut, flash surge and first kick on the same frame"))
    dur = T['meta']['duration']
    mid = (kt > dur * 0.4) & (kt < dur * 0.6)
    dn = np.array([np.min(np.abs(beats[down] - x)) < 0.03 for x in kt])
    cand = np.where(mid & dn)[0]
    if len(cand):
        j = cand[np.argmax(ks[cand])]
        spots.append((kt[j], 'strong downbeat kick mid-song - kick hit (scale punch + shockwave refraction) on this exact frame'))
    late = [s for s in S[1:] if s['label'] not in ('outro',)]
    if late:
        spots.append((late[-1]['start'], f"{late[-1]['label']} {late[-1]['occurrence']} boundary - transition lands on the downbeat"))
    L.append('## Spot-check timestamps')
    for t, what in spots:
        L.append(f"- **{mmss(t)}** (frame {int(round(t * fps))}) - {what}")
    if V:
        L.append('\n## Sync verification (measured on the delivered file)')
        for k in ['kick', 'beat', 'downbeat', 'snare', 'hat', 'section']:
            r = V.get(k)
            if r:
                L.append(f"- {k}: visual response peaks at lag **{r['peak_lag']:+d} frames** ({r['n']} events, contrast {r['contrast']}x)")
        if V.get('beats_with_visible_hit') is not None:
            L.append(f"- mute test proxy: {V['beats_with_visible_hit'] * 100:.0f}% of beats (in non-silent passages) carry a visible hit on their frame")
        for k, r in V.get('av_offset', {}).items():
            L.append(f"- audio vs source at {k} ({r['at_s']} s): {r['lag_samples']} samples ({r['lag_ms']} ms)")
        L.append(f"- photosensitivity: max {V.get('max_flashes_per_second')} flash(es) per second over any 25%-area region (limit 3)")
        L.append('- checks: ' + ', '.join(f"{k}: {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}" for k, ok in V.get('checks', {}).items()))
    open(a.out, 'w').write('\n'.join(L) + '\n')
    print('wrote', a.out)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

I've updated the `music-visualizer` skill with your five rules. It's in `~/.claude/skills/music-visualizer/`, and I backed up the old version to `scratchpad/music-visualizer.bak`. I tested it by rendering the example scene against the Bad Boys analysis: the rendered stills show only the title and artist, the oscilloscope appears in the intro, and the title-only ending looks clean. The analysis step also correctly read "Night Blur" from the file name.

**1. Title sets the theme.** The rules at the top of `SKILL.md` and step 1 of the design playbook now make the title the brief. The agent writes down the title's literal and figurative meaning (translating it if needed, e.g. Ngizula means "I wander"), picks a world from it, and takes the palette and motif from that world. The genre and mood of the audio only set energy and pacing. `analyze.py` takes the title from what you specify, then the file's tags, then the file name, which it now cleans up:
- `03_night-blur (master v2).wav` becomes "Night-Blur" (the hyphen stays)
- `EVENT_HORIZON_v3.flac` becomes "Event Horizon"
- `voho - Event Horizon.mp3` gives title "Event Horizon" and artist "voho"
- With no artist anywhere, the video shows the title alone.

**2. Cover image.** The agent uses a cover you give it, or art embedded in the song file. The new `scripts/cover_palette.py` extracts the cover's main colours, suggests a role for each (background, main colour, highlight, accent), and saves a swatch image next to the cover. The cover refines the title's world rather than replacing it: if they clash, the video keeps the title's world and uses the cover's colours.

**3. Only title and artist as text.** This is now a hard rule in `SKILL.md`, the playbook and the example scene. There are no lyrics, slogans, section names, "RUSH ×2"-style words or numbers. Repeated drops escalate with visuals instead, such as more rings bursting out. The contact-sheet review step now includes checking that no other text appears.

**4. No BPM or beat counters.** I removed the whole corner overlay from the example scene: STAGE, SCORE, COMBO, BPM and the beat lamps. I also removed the score and combo counters from the analysis layer. Build-ups now show tension with a ring closing in to meet the motif on the drop, instead of 3-2-1 numbers. Sections that lack visible beat hits should get a pulse on a large scene element, never a counter.

**5. Spectrogram or oscilloscope as a starting point.**
- **New waveform helper:** `tl.wave()` returns the live waveform for any frame. It is triggered like a hardware scope so steady tones hold still, and it can also return left/right channels for Lissajous figures.
- **Playbook recipes:** a new playbook section covers ways to use the spectrogram and oscilloscope as the base of the scene, and to build the song's world around them.
- **Example scene:** it now draws a live oscilloscope inside the intro reticle.

**Also added:** the two fixes the agents discovered are now in the skill's environment notes: the numba cache setting that stops analysis crashing, and the thread limit that took renders from about 5 fps to about 20–30 fps.

**Not done:** the four agents also patched the analysis to handle missed kicks and sections cut into slivers. They made those fixes separately in each song's work folder, and I haven't merged them into the skill's `analyze.py`. Consolidating them would stop the next song from needing the same patches. I can do that next if you want.
